segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.1
1. Impermanence
The Interior as Impermanent
So I have heard.

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, the eye is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: Yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
The ear is impermanent. …
The nose is impermanent. …
The tongue is impermanent. …

segs.p: Yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.

segs.e: The body is impermanent. …
The mind is impermanent.
What’s impermanent is suffering.
What’s suffering is not-self.

segs.p: Yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati, ghānasmimpi nibbindati, jivhāyapi nibbindati, kāyasmimpi nibbindati, manasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.7
1. Impermanence
The Interior as Impermanent in the Three Times
“Mendicants, the eye of the past and future is impermanent,
let alone the present.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṁ cakkhusmiṁ anapekkho hoti;
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple is not concerned with the eye of the past,
they don’t look forward to enjoying the eye in the future,

segs.p: paccuppannassa cakkhussa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: and they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the eye in the present.
The ear …
nose …
tongue …

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītāya jivhāya anapekkho hoti;
paccuppannāya jivhāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

segs.e: body …
mind of the past and future is impermanent,
let alone the present.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṁ manasmiṁ anapekkho hoti;
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple doesn’t worry about the mind of the past,
they don’t look forward to enjoying the mind in the future,

segs.p: paccuppannassa manassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: and they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the mind in the present.”

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.13
2. Pairs
Before My Awakening (Interior)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho cakkhussa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: ‘What’s the gratification, the drawback, and the escape when it comes to the eye …
ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …

segs.p: ko manassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: and mind?’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho cakkhuṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ cakkhussa assādo.
segs.e: ‘The pleasure and happiness that arise from the eye: this is its gratification.

segs.p: Yaṁ cakkhuṁ aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, ayaṁ cakkhussa ādīnavo.
segs.e: That the eye is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

segs.p: Yo cakkhusmiṁ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ cakkhussa nissaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Removing and giving up desire and greed for the eye: this is its escape.
The pleasure and happiness that arise from the ear …
nose …

segs.p: yaṁ jivhaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ jivhāya assādo.
segs.e: tongue …

segs.p: Yaṁ jivhā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ jivhāya ādīnavo.
Yo jivhāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ jivhāya nissaraṇaṁ.

segs.e: body …

segs.p: yaṁ manaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ manassa assādo.
segs.e: mind: this is its gratification.

segs.p: Yaṁ mano anicco dukkho vipariṇāmadhammo, ayaṁ manassa ādīnavo.
segs.e: That the mind is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

segs.p: Yo manasmiṁ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ manassa nissaraṇan’ti.
segs.e: Removing and giving up desire and greed for the mind: this is its escape.’

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ, neva tāvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: As long as I didn’t truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

segs.p: Yato ca khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, athāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
segs.e: But when I did truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.
Knowledge and vision arose in me:

segs.p: ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”
Linked Discourses 35.14
2. Pairs
Before My Awakening (Exterior)

segs.p: “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘ko nu kho rūpānaṁ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: ‘What’s the gratification, the drawback, and the escape when it comes to sights …
sounds …
smells …
tastes …
touches …

segs.p: ko dhammānaṁ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: and ideas?’ …”

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho rūpe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ rūpānaṁ assādo.
Yaṁ rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ rūpānaṁ ādīnavo.
Yo rūpesu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ rūpānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ.
yaṁ dhamme paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ dhammānaṁ assādo.
Yaṁ dhammā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ dhammānaṁ ādīnavo.
Yo dhammesu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ dhammānaṁ nissaraṇan’ti.

Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ bāhirānaṁ āyatanānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ, neva tāvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.

Yato ca khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ bāhirānaṁ āyatanānaṁ evaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, athāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṁ.
‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.15
2. Pairs
In Search of Gratification (Interior)
“Mendicants, I went in search of the eye’s gratification,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā cakkhussa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of the eye’s gratification.
I went in search of the eye’s drawback,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā cakkhussa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of the eye’s drawback.
I went in search of escape from the eye,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā cakkhussa nissaraṇaṁ, paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of escape from the eye.
I went in search of the ear’s …
nose’s …
tongue’s …

segs.p: Yāvatā jivhāya assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā jivhāya ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā jivhāya nissaraṇaṁ, paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ …pe…
segs.e: body’s …
mind’s gratification,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā manassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of the mind’s gratification.
I went in search of the mind’s drawback,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā manassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of the mind’s drawback.
I went in search of escape from the mind,
and I found it.

segs.p: Yāvatā manassa nissaraṇaṁ, paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve seen clearly with wisdom the full extent of escape from the mind.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ …pe…
segs.e: As long as I didn’t truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening …
But when I did truly understand …
Knowledge and vision arose in me:

segs.p: ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”
Linked Discourses 35.16
2. Pairs

“Mendicants, I went in search of the gratification of sights,
and I found it. …”

segs.p: Yāvatā rūpānaṁ assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā rūpānaṁ ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā rūpānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ, paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
Yāvatā dhammānaṁ assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā dhammānaṁ ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho.
Yāvatā dhammānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ, paññāya me taṁ sudiṭṭhaṁ.
Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ channaṁ bāhirānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññāsiṁ …pe… paccaññāsiṁ.
‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.17
2. Pairs
If There Were No Gratification (Interior)

segs.p: “No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā cakkhusmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if there were no gratification in the eye, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa assādo tasmā sattā cakkhusmiṁ sārajjanti.
segs.e: But since there is gratification in the eye, sentient beings are aroused by it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā cakkhusmiṁ nibbindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If the eye had no drawback, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa ādīnavo tasmā sattā cakkhusmiṁ nibbindanti.
segs.e: But since the eye has a drawback, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā cakkhusmā nissareyyuṁ.
segs.e: If there were no escape from the eye, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa nissaraṇaṁ tasmā sattā cakkhusmā nissaranti.
segs.e: But since there is an escape from the eye, sentient beings do escape from it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, sotassa assādo abhavissa …
segs.e: If there were no gratification in the ear …

segs.p: no cedaṁ, bhikkhave, ghānassa assādo abhavissa …
segs.e: nose …

segs.p: no cedaṁ, bhikkhave, jivhāya assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā jivhāya sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: tongue …

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya assādo, tasmā sattā jivhāya sārajjanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, jivhāya ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā jivhāya nibbindeyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya ādīnavo, tasmā sattā jivhāya nibbindanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, jivhāya nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā jivhāya nissareyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā jivhāya nissaranti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, kāyassa assādo abhavissa …
segs.e: body …

segs.p: no cedaṁ, bhikkhave, manassa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā manasmiṁ sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: mind, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa assādo, tasmā sattā manasmiṁ sārajjanti.
segs.e: But since there is gratification in the mind, sentient beings are aroused by it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, manassa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā manasmiṁ nibbindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If the mind had no drawback, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā manasmiṁ nibbindanti.
segs.e: But since the mind has a drawback, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, manassa nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā manasmā nissareyyuṁ.
segs.e: If there were no escape from the mind, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā manasmā nissaranti.
segs.e: But since there is an escape from the mind, sentient beings do escape from it.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ channaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññaṁsu, neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā vihariṁsu.
segs.e: As long as sentient beings don’t truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they haven’t escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they don’t live detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ channaṁ ajjhattikānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññaṁsu, atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharantī”ti.
segs.e: But when sentient beings truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they’ve escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they live detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.”
Linked Discourses 35.18
2. Pairs

segs.p: “No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṁ assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā rūpesu sārajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if there were no gratification in sights, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by them. …”

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṁ assādo, tasmā sattā rūpesu sārajjanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṁ ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā rūpesu nibbindeyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṁ ādīnavo, tasmā sattā rūpesu nibbindanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā rūpehi nissareyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā rūpehi nissaranti.
dhammānaṁ assādo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā dhammesu sārajjeyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṁ assādo, tasmā sattā dhammesu sārajjanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā dhammesu nibbindeyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṁ ādīnavo, tasmā sattā dhammesu nibbindanti.
No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ abhavissa, nayidaṁ sattā dhammehi nissareyyuṁ.
Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ, tasmā sattā dhammehi nissaranti.

Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ channaṁ bāhirānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ nābbhaññaṁsu, neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā vihariṁsu.

Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṁ channaṁ bāhirānaṁ āyatanānaṁ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññaṁsu, atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharantī”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.19
2. Pairs

segs.p: “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhuṁ abhinandati, dukkhaṁ so abhinandati.

2. Pairs
The Arising of Suffering (Interior)

segs.p: “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhussa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṁ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.
The arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …

segs.p: yo manassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṁ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.
segs.e: and mind is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhussa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṁ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo.
segs.e: The cessation, settling, and disappearance of the eye is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.
The cessation, settling, and disappearance of the ear,
nose,
tongue,
body,

segs.p: yo manassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṁ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti.
segs.e: and mind is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.”

3. All
All
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you the all.
Listen …
And what is the all?

segs.p: Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañca saddā ca, ghānañca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca, kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca—
segs.e: It’s just the eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.
This is called the all.
Mendicants, suppose someone was to say:

segs.p: ‘ahametaṁ sabbaṁ paccakkhāya aññaṁ sabbaṁ paññāpessāmī’ti, tassa vācāvatthukamevassa;
segs.e: ‘I’ll deny this all and describe another all.’ They’d have no grounds for that claim,

segs.p: puṭṭho ca na sampāyeyya, uttariñca vighātaṁ āpajjeyya.
segs.e: they’d be stumped by questions, and, in addition, they’d get frustrated.
Why is that?
Because they’re out of their element.”
Linked Discourses 35.24
3. All
Giving Up
“Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for giving up the all.
Listen …
And what is the principle for giving up the all?

segs.p: Cakkhuṁ, bhikkhave, pahātabbaṁ, rūpā pahātabbā, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ pahātabbaṁ, cakkhusamphasso pahātabbo, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi pahātabbaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The eye should be given up. Sights should be given up. Eye consciousness should be given up. Eye contact should be given up. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact should also be given up.
The ear … nose …

segs.p: jivhā pahātabbā, rasā pahātabbā, jivhāviññāṇaṁ pahātabbaṁ, jivhāsamphasso pahātabbo, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi pahātabbaṁ.
segs.e: tongue …
body …

segs.p: mano pahātabbo, dhammā pahātabbā, manoviññāṇaṁ pahātabbaṁ, manosamphasso pahātabbo, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi pahātabbaṁ.
segs.e: mind should be given up. Ideas should be given up. Mind consciousness should be given up. Mind contact should be given up. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact should be given up.
This is the principle for giving up the all.”
Linked Discourses 35.25
3. All
Giving Up By Direct Knowledge and Complete Understanding

segs.p: “Sabbaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desessāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for giving up the all by direct knowledge and complete understanding.
Listen …

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sabbaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya dhammo?
segs.e: And what is the principle for giving up the all by direct knowledge and complete understanding?

segs.p: Cakkhuṁ, bhikkhave, abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ, rūpā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ, cakkhusamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The eye should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Sights should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Eye consciousness should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Eye contact should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding.
The ear … nose …

segs.p: jivhā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, rasā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, jivhāviññāṇaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ, jivhāsamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ.
segs.e: tongue …
body …

segs.p: mano abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, dhammā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, manoviññāṇaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ, manosamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṁ.
segs.e: mind should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Ideas should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Mind consciousness should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. Mind contact should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact should be given up by direct knowledge and complete understanding.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṁ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya dhammo”ti.
segs.e: This is the principle for giving up the all by direct knowledge and complete understanding.”
Linked Discourses 35.26
3. All
Without Completely Understanding (1st)

segs.p: “Sabbaṁ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without directly knowing and completely understanding the all, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya?
segs.e: And what is the all, without directly knowing and completely understanding which, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuṁ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: Without directly knowing and completely understanding the eye, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: Rūpe anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: Without directly knowing and completely understanding sights …

segs.p: Cakkhuviññāṇaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: eye consciousness …

segs.p: Cakkhusamphassaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: eye contact …

segs.p: Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya …pe…
segs.e: painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: jivhaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: Without directly knowing and completely understanding the ear … the nose … the tongue …

segs.p: yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.

segs.e: the body …

segs.p: manaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: the mind, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.
Without directly knowing and completely understanding ideas …
mind consciousness …
mind contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṁ anabhijānaṁ aparijānaṁ avirājayaṁ appajahaṁ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: This is the all, without directly knowing and completely understanding which, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering.

segs.p: Sabbañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṁ parijānaṁ virājayaṁ pajahaṁ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: By directly knowing and completely understanding the all, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṁ abhijānaṁ parijānaṁ virājayaṁ pajahaṁ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya?
segs.e: And what is the all, directly knowing and completely understanding which, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuṁ, bhikkhave, abhijānaṁ parijānaṁ virājayaṁ pajahaṁ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.

3. All
Burning

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā gayāyaṁ viharati gayāsīse saddhiṁ bhikkhusahassena.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Gayā on Gayā Head together with a thousand mendicants.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:
“Mendicants, all is burning.
And what is the all that is burning?

segs.p: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, ādittaṁ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ ādittaṁ, cakkhusamphasso āditto. Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi ādittaṁ.
segs.e: The eye is burning. Sights are burning. Eye consciousness is burning. Eye contact is burning. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also burning.
Burning with what?

segs.p: ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṁ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittan’ti vadāmi …pe…
segs.e: Burning with the fires of greed, hate, and delusion. Burning with rebirth, old age, and death, with sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: jivhā ādittā, rasā ādittā, jivhāviññāṇaṁ ādittaṁ, jivhāsamphasso āditto. Yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi ādittaṁ.
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṁ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittan’ti vadāmi …pe…
mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, manoviññāṇaṁ ādittaṁ, manosamphasso āditto. Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi ādittaṁ.
segs.e: The mind is burning. Ideas are burning. Mind consciousness is burning. Mind contact is burning. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also burning.
Burning with what?

segs.p: ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṁ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittan’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Burning with the fires of greed, hate, and delusion. Burning with rebirth, old age, and death, with sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanduṁ.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhusahassassa anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṁsūti.
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the thousand mendicants were freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: ‘Jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi addhabhūtan’ti vadāmi.

segs.e: body …

segs.p: mano addhabhūto, dhammā addhabhūtā, manoviññāṇaṁ addhabhūtaṁ, manosamphasso addhabhūto, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi addhabhūtaṁ.
segs.e: mind is overcome. Ideas are overcome. Mind consciousness is overcome. Mind contact is overcome. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also overcome.

segs.p: ‘Jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi addhabhūtan’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Overcome by greed, hate, and delusion. Overcome by rebirth, old age, and death, by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, I say.

segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṁ ‘vimuttam’iti ñāṇaṁ hoti,
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

3. All
The Practice Fit for Uprooting
“Mendicants, I will teach you the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmīti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

segs.p: Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, sabbamaññitasamugghātasāruppā paṭipadā?
segs.e: And what is the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuṁ na maññati, cakkhusmiṁ na maññati, cakkhuto na maññati, cakkhuṁ meti na maññati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant does not conceive anything to be the eye, does not conceive it in the eye, does not conceive it as the eye, and does not conceive that ‘the eye is mine.’

segs.p: Rūpe na maññati, rūpesu na maññati, rūpato na maññati, rūpā meti na maññati.
segs.e: They don’t conceive anything to be sights, they don’t conceive it in sights, they don’t conceive it as sights, and they don’t conceive that ‘sights are mine.’

segs.p: Cakkhuviññāṇaṁ na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇasmiṁ na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇato na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ meti na maññati.
segs.e: They don’t conceive eye consciousness …

segs.p: Cakkhusamphassaṁ na maññati, cakkhusamphassasmiṁ na maññati, cakkhusamphassato na maññati, cakkhusamphasso meti na maññati.
segs.e: eye contact …

segs.p: Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṁ meti na maññati …pe…
segs.e: They don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: jivhaṁ na maññati, jivhāya na maññati, jivhāto na maññati, jivhā meti na maññati.
segs.e: They don’t conceive anything to be the ear … nose … tongue …

segs.p: Rase na maññati, rasesu na maññati, rasato na maññati, rasā meti na maññati.
Jivhāviññāṇaṁ na maññati, jivhāviññāṇasmiṁ na maññati, jivhāviññāṇato na maññati, jivhāviññāṇaṁ meti na maññati.
Jivhāsamphassaṁ na maññati, jivhāsamphassasmiṁ na maññati, jivhāsamphassato na maññati, jivhāsamphasso meti na maññati.
Yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṁ meti na maññati …pe…
segs.e: body …

segs.p: manaṁ na maññati, manasmiṁ na maññati, manato na maññati, mano meti na maññati.
segs.e: mind …

segs.p: Dhamme na maññati, dhammesu na maññati, dhammato na maññati, dhammā meti na maññati.
Manoviññāṇaṁ na maññati, manoviññāṇasmiṁ na maññati, manoviññāṇato na maññati, manoviññāṇaṁ meti na maññati.
Manosamphassaṁ na maññati, manosamphassasmiṁ na maññati, manosamphassato na maññati, manosamphasso meti na maññati.
Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṁ meti na maññati.
segs.e: They don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: Sabbaṁ na maññati, sabbasmiṁ na maññati, sabbato na maññati, sabbaṁ meti na maññati.
segs.e: They don’t conceive anything to be all, they don’t conceive it in all, they don’t conceive it as all, and they don’t conceive that ‘all is mine.’

segs.p: So evaṁ amaññamāno na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
segs.e: Not conceiving, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

segs.p: Anupādiyaṁ na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, sabbamaññitasamugghātasāruppā paṭipadā”ti.
segs.e: This is the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving.”

segs.e: mind …

segs.p: manoviññāṇaṁ na maññati, manosamphassaṁ na maññati.
Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṁ meti na maññati.

6. Ignorance
The Complete Understanding of All Grasping
“Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for the complete understanding of all grasping.

And what is the principle for the complete understanding of all grasping?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati.

segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely understood grasping.’

Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely depleted fuel for grasping.’
This is the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping.”

6. Ignorance
The Depletion of All Fuel for Grasping (2nd)
“Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping.
Listen …
And what is the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping?
What do you think, mendicants?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati.
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: jivhāyapi nibbindati, rasesupi nibbindati, jivhāviññāṇepi nibbindati, jivhāsamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati …pe…
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manasmimpi nibbindati, dhammesupi nibbindati, manoviññāṇepi nibbindati, manosamphassepi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.

7. With Migajāla
With Migajāla (1st)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā migajālo yena bhagavā …pe…
segs.e: Then Venerable Migajāla went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā migajālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of one who lives alone.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ekavihārī hoti, kittāvatā ca pana sadutiyavihārī hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is one who lives alone defined? And how is living with a partner defined?”

segs.p: “Santi kho, migajāla, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Migajāla, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
When there’s relishing there’s lust.
When there’s lust there is yoking.

segs.p: Nandisaṁyojanasaṁyutto kho, migajāla, bhikkhu sadutiyavihārīti vuccati.
segs.e: A mendicant who is fettered by relishing is said to live with a partner.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Santi kho, migajāla, jivhāviññeyyā rasā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
When there’s relishing there’s lust.
When there’s lust there is yoking.

segs.p: Nandisaṁyojanasaṁyutto kho, migajāla, bhikkhu sadutiyavihārīti vuccati.
segs.e: A mendicant who is fettered by relishing is said to live with a partner.

segs.p: Evaṁvihārī ca, migajāla, bhikkhu kiñcāpi araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni;
segs.e: A mendicant who lives like this is said to live with a partner, even if they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest that are quiet and still, far from the madding crowd, remote from human settlements, and fit for retreat.
Why is that?
For craving is their partner, and they haven’t given it up.
That’s why they’re said to live with a partner.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, migajāla, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nandī nirujjhati.
segs.e: relishing ceases.
When there’s no relishing there’s no lust.
When there’s no lust there’s no yoking.

segs.p: Nandisaṁyojanavisaṁyutto kho, migajāla, bhikkhu ekavihārīti vuccati …pe…
segs.e: A mendicant who is not fettered by relishing is said to live alone.

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
segs.e: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nandī nirujjhati.
segs.e: relishing ceases.
When there’s no relishing there’s no lust.
When there’s no lust there’s no yoking.

segs.p: Nandisaṁyojanavippayutto kho, migajāla, bhikkhu ekavihārīti vuccati.
segs.e: A mendicant who is not fettered by relishing is said to live alone.

segs.p: Evaṁvihārī ca, migajāla, bhikkhu kiñcāpi gāmante viharati ākiṇṇo bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives like this is said to live alone, even if they live within a village crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and monastics of other religions and their disciples.
Why is that?
For craving is their partner, and they have given it up.
That’s why they’re said to live alone.”

7. With Migajāla
With Migajāla (2nd)

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā migajālo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: Then Venerable Migajāla went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā migajālo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Santi kho, migajāla, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Migajāla, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
segs.e: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, migajāla, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nandī nirujjhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.
When relishing ceases, suffering ceases, I say.

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, jivhāviññeyyā rasā iṭṭhā kantā …pe…
segs.e: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi ca kho, migajāla, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nandī nirujjhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.
When relishing ceases, suffering ceases, I say.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā migajālo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And then Venerable Migajāla approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā migajālo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharato nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Migajāla, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā migajālo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Migajāla became one of the perfected.

7. With Migajāla
Samiddhi’s Question About Māra

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi yena bhagavā …pe…
segs.e: Then Venerable Samiddhi went up to the Buddha …
and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘Māra’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, māro vā assa mārapaññatti vā”ti?
segs.e: How do we define Māra or what is known as Māra?”

segs.p: “Yattha kho, samiddhi, atthi cakkhu, atthi rūpā, atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, atthi cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: “Samiddhi, where there is the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and things knowable by eye consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Atthi sotaṁ, atthi saddā, atthi sotaviññāṇaṁ, atthi sotaviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is the ear, sounds, ear consciousness, and things knowable by ear consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Atthi ghānaṁ, atthi gandhā, atthi ghānaviññāṇaṁ, atthi ghānaviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is the nose, smells, nose consciousness, and things knowable by nose consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Atthi jivhā, atthi rasā, atthi jivhāviññāṇaṁ, atthi jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is the tongue, tastes, tongue consciousness, and things knowable by tongue consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Atthi kāyo, atthi phoṭṭhabbā, atthi kāyaviññāṇaṁ, atthi kāyaviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is the body, touches, body consciousness, and things knowable by body consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Atthi mano, atthi dhammā, atthi manoviññāṇaṁ, atthi manoviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, atthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and things knowable by mind consciousness, there is Māra or what is known as Māra.

segs.p: Yattha ca kho, samiddhi, natthi cakkhu, natthi rūpā, natthi cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, natthi cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, natthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: Where there is no eye, no sights, no eye consciousness, and no things knowable by eye consciousness, there is no Māra or what is known as Māra.
Where there is no ear …
no nose …

segs.p: natthi jivhā, natthi rasā, natthi jivhāviññāṇaṁ, natthi jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, natthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā.
segs.e: no tongue …
no body …

segs.p: Natthi mano, natthi dhammā, natthi manoviññāṇaṁ, natthi manoviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā, natthi tattha māro vā mārapaññatti vā”ti.
segs.e: Where there is no mind, no ideas, no mind consciousness, and no things knowable by mind consciousness, there is no Māra or what is known as Māra.”

7. With Migajāla
Upasena and the Viper

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca upaseno rājagahe viharanti sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre.
segs.e: At one time the venerables Sāriputta and Upasena were staying near Rājagaha in the Cool Grove, under the Cobra’s Hood Grotto.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upasenassa kāye āsīviso patito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a viper fell on Upasena’s body.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā upaseno bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: He addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “etha me, āvuso, imaṁ kāyaṁ mañcakaṁ āropetvā bahiddhā nīharatha.
segs.e: “Come, reverends, lift this body onto a cot and carry it outside
before it’s scattered right here
like a handful of hay.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ upasenaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Sāriputta said to him,

segs.p: “na kho pana mayaṁ passāma āyasmato upasenassa kāyassa vā aññathattaṁ indriyānaṁ vā vipariṇāmaṁ.
segs.e: “But we don’t see any impairment in your body or deterioration of your faculties.
Yet you say:

segs.p: ‘etha me, āvuso, imaṁ kāyaṁ mañcakaṁ āropetvā bahiddhā nīharatha.
segs.e: ‘Come, reverends, lift this body onto a cot and carry it outside
before it’s scattered right here
like a handful of hay.’”
“Reverend Sāriputta, there may be an impairment in body or deterioration of faculties for someone who thinks:
‘I am the eye’ or ‘the eye is mine.’

segs.p: ahaṁ jivhāti vā mama jivhāti vā …
segs.e: Or ‘I am the ear … nose … tongue … body …’

segs.p: ahaṁ manoti vā mama mano’ti vā.
segs.e: Or ‘I am the mind’ or ‘the mind is mine.’

segs.p: Tassa, āvuso sāriputta, siyā kāyassa vā aññathattaṁ indriyānaṁ vā vipariṇāmo.
Mayhañca kho, āvuso sāriputta, na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: But I don’t think like that.

segs.p: ahaṁ jivhāti vā mama jivhāti vā …pe…
ahaṁ manoti vā mama manoti vā’.
Tassa mayhañca kho, āvuso sāriputta, kiṁ kāyassa vā aññathattaṁ bhavissati, indriyānaṁ vā vipariṇāmo”ti.
segs.e: So why would there be an impairment in my body or deterioration of my faculties?”

segs.p: Tathā hi panāyasmato upasenassa dīgharattaṁ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayo susamūhato.
segs.e: “That must be because Venerable Upasena has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

segs.p: Tasmā āyasmato upasenassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: That’s why it doesn’t occur to you:
‘I am the eye’ or ‘the eye is mine.’ Or ‘I am the ear …

segs.p: ahaṁ jivhāti vā mama jivhāti vā …pe…
segs.e: nose … tongue … body …’

segs.p: ahaṁ manoti vā mama mano’ti vā”ti.
segs.e: Or ‘I am the mind’ or ‘the mind is mine.’”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmato upasenassa kāyaṁ mañcakaṁ āropetvā bahiddhā nīhariṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants lifted Upasena’s body onto a cot and carried it outside.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato upasenassa kāyo tattheva vikiri;
segs.e: And his body was scattered right there
like a handful of hay.

7. With Migajāla
Upavāṇa on What is Apparent in the Present Life

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā upavāṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: Then Venerable Upavāṇa went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of ‘a teaching apparent in the present life’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti, akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti?
segs.e: In what way is the teaching apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves?”

segs.p: “Idha pana, upavāṇa, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā rūpappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti rūparāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: “Upavāṇa, take a mendicant who sees a sight with their eyes. They experience both the sight and the desire for the sight.

segs.p: Santañca ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: There is desire for sights in them, and they understand that.

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā rūpappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti rūparāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: Since this is so,

segs.p: Santañca ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
Evampi kho, upavāṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhi …pe….
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā rasappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti rasarāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who hears … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Santañca ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
Yaṁ taṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā rasappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti rasarāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
Santañca ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgo’ti pajānāti. Evampi kho, upavāṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhi …pe….
Puna caparaṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya dhammappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammarāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who knows an idea with their mind. They experience both the idea and the desire for the idea.

segs.p: Santañca ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: There is desire for ideas in them, and they understand that.

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya dhammappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammarāgappaṭisaṁvedī ca.
segs.e: Since this is so,

segs.p: Santañca ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
Evampi kho, upavāṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhi …pe….
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Idha pana, upavāṇa, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā rūpappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti, no ca rūparāgappaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who sees a sight with their eyes. They experience the sight but no desire for the sight.

segs.p: Asantañca ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: There is no desire for sights in them, and they understand that.

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā rūpappaṭisaṁvedīhi kho hoti, no ca rūparāgappaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: Since this is so,

segs.p: Asantañca ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ rūpesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
Evampi kho, upavāṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti, akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhi …pe….
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā rasappaṭisaṁvedīhi kho hoti, no ca rasarāgappaṭisaṁvedī. Asantañca ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ rasesu rāgo’ti pajānāti …pe….
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who hears … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya dhammappaṭisaṁvedīhi kho hoti, no ca dhammarāgappaṭisaṁvedī.
Asantañca ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
Yaṁ taṁ, upavāṇa, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya dhammappaṭisaṁvedīhi kho hoti, no ca dhammarāgappaṭisaṁvedī.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who knows an idea with their mind. They experience the idea but no desire for the idea.

segs.p: Asantañca ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammesu rāgo’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: There is no desire for ideas in them, and they understand that.

segs.p: Evampi kho, upavāṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti, akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.
segs.e: Since this is so, this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

7. With Migajāla
Six Fields of Contact (1st)

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, anyone who doesn’t truly understand the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape

segs.p: Avusitaṁ tena brahmacariyaṁ, ārakā so imasmā dhammavinayā”ti.
segs.e: has not completed the spiritual journey and is far from this teaching and training.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,
“Here, sir, I’m discouraged.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmī”ti.
segs.e: For I don’t truly understand the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.”
“What do you think, mendicant?

segs.p: cakkhuṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you regard the eye like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhu, ettha ca te, bhikkhu, cakkhu ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: “Good, mendicant! And regarding the eye, you will truly see clearly with right wisdom that: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
Just this is the end of suffering.

segs.p: jivhaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you regard the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhu, ettha ca te, bhikkhu, jivhā ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ bhavissati.
manaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you regard the mind like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhu, ettha ca te, bhikkhu, mano ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: “Good, mendicant! And regarding the mind, you will truly see clearly with right wisdom that: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
Just this is the end of suffering.”

segs.p: Evaṁ te etaṁ paṭhamaṁ phassāyatanaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati āyatiṁ apunabbhavāya …pe….

segs.p: “Jivhaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhu, ettha ca te, bhikkhu, jivhā ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ bhavissati. Evaṁ te etaṁ catutthaṁ phassāyatanaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati āyatiṁ apunabbhavāya …pe….
“Manaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: Do you regard the mind like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhu, ettha ca te, bhikkhu, mano ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: “Good, mendicant! And regarding the mind, you will truly see clearly with right wisdom that: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ te etaṁ chaṭṭhaṁ phassāyatanaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati āyatiṁ apunabbhavāyā”ti.
segs.e: In this way you will give up the sixth field of contact, so that there are no more future lives.”

7. With Migajāla
Six Fields of Contact (3rd)

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, anyone who doesn’t truly understand the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape

segs.p: Avusitaṁ tena brahmacariyaṁ, ārakā so imasmā dhammavinayā”ti.
segs.e: has not completed the spiritual journey and is far from this teaching and training.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,
“Here, sir, I’m discouraged, really discouraged.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmī”ti.
segs.e: For I don’t truly understand the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.”
“What do you think, mendicant?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …
mind permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati, ghānasmimpi nibbindati, jivhāyapi nibbindati, kāyasmimpi nibbindati, manasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

8. Sick
Sick (1st)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, and said to him,

segs.p: “amukasmiṁ, bhante, vihāre aññataro bhikkhu navo appaññāto ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: “Sir, in such-and-such monastery there’s a mendicant who is junior and not well-known. He’s sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please go to him out of sympathy.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā navavādañca sutvā gilānavādañca, “appaññāto bhikkhū”ti iti viditvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: When the Buddha heard that the mendicant was junior and ill, understanding that he was not well-known, he went to him.

segs.p: Addasā kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: That mendicant saw the Buddha coming off in the distance
and stirred in his cot.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to that monk,
“It’s all right, mendicant, don’t get up.
There are some seats spread out, I will sit there.”
He sat down on the seat spread out

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to the mendicant,

segs.p: “kacci te, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, mendicant, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

segs.p: “Kacci te, bhikkhu, na kiñci kukkuccaṁ, na koci vippaṭisāro”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you don’t have any remorse or regret?”

segs.p: “Taggha me, bhante, anappakaṁ kukkuccaṁ, anappako vippaṭisāro”ti.
segs.e: “Indeed, sir, I have no little remorse and regret.”

segs.p: “Kacci pana taṁ, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you have no reason to blame yourself when it comes to ethical conduct?”

segs.p: “Na kho maṁ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.
segs.e: “No sir, I have no reason to blame myself when it comes to ethical conduct.”

segs.p: “No ce kira te, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca te kukkuccaṁ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?
segs.e: “In that case, mendicant, why do you have remorse and regret?”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ, bhante, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Because I understand that the Buddha has not taught the Dhamma merely for the sake of ethical purity.”

segs.p: “No ce kira tvaṁ, bhikkhu, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi, atha kimatthaṁ carahi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsī”ti?
segs.e: “If that is so, what then do you understand to be the purpose of teaching the Dhamma?”

segs.p: “Rāgavirāgatthaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I understand that the Buddha has taught the Dhamma for the purpose of the fading away of greed.”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, rāgavirāgatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi.
segs.e: It’s good that you understand that I’ve taught the Dhamma for the purpose of the fading away of greed.

segs.p: Rāgavirāgattho hi, bhikkhu, mayā dhammo desito.
segs.e: For that is indeed the purpose.
What do you think, mendicant?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …
“Is the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …
mind permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati …pe… manasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.
They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamano so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandi.
segs.e: Satisfied, that mendicant approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhuno virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in that mendicant:
“Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

8. Sick
Sick (2nd)

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu …pe… bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “amukasmiṁ, bhante, vihāre aññataro bhikkhu navo appaññāto ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: “Sir, in such-and-such monastery there’s a mendicant who is junior and not well-known. He’s sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please go to him out of sympathy.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā navavādañca sutvā gilānavādañca, “appaññāto bhikkhū”ti iti viditvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: When the Buddha heard that the mendicant was junior and ill, understanding that he was not well-known, he went to him.

segs.p: Addasā kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: That mendicant saw the Buddha coming off in the distance
and stirred in his cot.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to that monk,
“It’s all right, mendicant, don’t get up.
There are some seats spread out, I will sit there.”

segs.p: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He sat down on the seat spread out and said to the mendicant,

segs.p: “kacci te, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, mendicant, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”
“Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. …

segs.p: na kho maṁ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.
segs.e: I have no reason to blame myself when it comes to ethical conduct.”

segs.p: “No ce kira te, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca te kukkuccaṁ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?
segs.e: “In that case, mendicant, why do you have remorse and regret?”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ, bhante, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Because I understand that the Buddha has not taught the Dhamma merely for the sake of ethical purity.”

segs.p: “No ce kira tvaṁ, bhikkhu, sīlavisuddhatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi, atha kimatthaṁ carahi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsī”ti?
segs.e: “If that is so, what then do you understand to be the goal of teaching the Dhamma?”

segs.p: “Anupādāparinibbānatthaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I understand that the Buddha has taught the Dhamma for the goal of complete extinguishment without grasping fuel.”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, anupādāparinibbānatthaṁ mayā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāsi.
segs.e: It’s good that you understand that I’ve taught the Dhamma for the goal of complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.

segs.p: Anupādāparinibbānattho hi, bhikkhu, mayā dhammo desito.
segs.e: For that is indeed the goal.
What do you think, mendicant?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …
“Is the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …
mind …
mind consciousness …
mind contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye … ear … nose … tongue … body …
mind …
mind consciousness …
mind contact …

segs.p: Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamano so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandi.
segs.e: Satisfied, that mendicant approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhussa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccīti.
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, the mind of that mendicant was freed from defilements by not grasping.

8. Sick
With Rādha on Impermanence
Then Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him,

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up desire for what is impermanent.

segs.p: Kiñca, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo?
segs.e: And what is impermanent?
The eye, sights, eye consciousness,
and eye contact are impermanent.

segs.p: yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
segs.e: And the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also impermanent. You should give up desire for it.
The ear … nose … tongue …
body …

segs.p: mano anicco. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
segs.e: The mind,
ideas,
mind consciousness,
and mind contact are impermanent.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
segs.e: And the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also impermanent. You should give up desire for it.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should give up desire for what is impermanent.”

8. Sick
With Rādha on Suffering

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up desire for what is suffering. …”

segs.p: Cakkhu kho, rādha, dukkhaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassa …pe… adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
Yaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhaṁ tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti.

8. Sick
With Rādha on Not-Self

segs.p: “Yo kho, rādha, anattā tatra te chando pahātabbo.
segs.e: “Rādha, you should give up desire for what is not-self. …”

segs.p: Cakkhu kho, rādha, anattā. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anattā. Tatra te chando pahātabbo.
Yo kho, rādha, anattā tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti.
