8. Sick
Giving Up Ignorance (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe…
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him:

segs.p: “atthi nu kho, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, is there one thing such that by giving it up a mendicant gives up ignorance and gives rise to knowledge?”

segs.p: “Atthi kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: “There is, mendicant.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But what is that one thing?”

segs.p: “Avijjā kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: “Ignorance is one thing such that by giving it up a mendicant gives up ignorance and gives rise to knowledge.”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ pana, bhante, jānato, kathaṁ passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But how does a mendicant know and see so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge?”

segs.p: “Cakkhuṁ kho, bhikkhu, aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Rūpe … cakkhuviññāṇaṁ … cakkhusamphassaṁ …
segs.e: “When a mendicant knows and sees the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

segs.p: yampidaṁ, cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati …pe…
segs.e: And also knowing and seeing the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises. …

segs.p: manaṁ aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Dhamme … manoviññāṇaṁ … manosamphassaṁ …
segs.e: Knowing and seeing the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati.
segs.e: And also knowing and seeing the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṁ passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant knows and sees so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge.”

8. Sick
Giving Up Ignorance (2nd)
Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “atthi nu kho, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, is there one thing such that by giving it up a mendicant gives up ignorance and gives rise to knowledge?”

segs.p: “Atthi kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: “There is, mendicant.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But what is that one thing?”

segs.p: “Avijjā kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: “Ignorance is one thing such that by giving it up a mendicant gives up ignorance and gives rise to knowledge.”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ pana, bhante, jānato, kathaṁ passato avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But how does a mendicant know and see so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge?”
“Take a mendicant who has heard:
‘Nothing is worth insisting on.’
When a mendicant has heard that
nothing is worth insisting on,

segs.p: So sabbaṁ dhammaṁ abhijānāti, sabbaṁ dhammaṁ abhiññāya sabbaṁ dhammaṁ parijānāti, sabbaṁ dhammaṁ pariññāya sabbanimittāni aññato passati, cakkhuṁ aññato passati, rūpe …
segs.e: they directly know all things. Directly knowing all things, they completely understand all things. Completely understanding all things, they see all signs as other. They see the eye, sights,
eye consciousness,
and eye contact as other.

segs.p: yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aññato passati …pe…
segs.e: And they also see the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact as other. …
They see the mind, ideas,
mind consciousness,
and mind contact as other.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aññato passati.
segs.e: And they also see the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact as other.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṁ passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant knows and sees so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge.”

8. Sick
Several Mendicants

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “idha no, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā amhe evaṁ pucchanti:
segs.e: “Sir, sometimes wanderers of other religions ask us:
‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā mayaṁ, bhante, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākaroma:
segs.e: We answer them like this:

segs.p: ‘dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññatthaṁ bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand suffering.’

segs.p: Kacci mayaṁ, bhante, evaṁ puṭṭhā evaṁ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva bhagavato homa, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaroma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchatī”ti?
segs.e: Answering this way, we trust that we repeat what the Buddha has said, and don’t misrepresent him with an untruth. We trust our explanation is in line with the teaching, and that there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

segs.p: “Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ puṭṭhā evaṁ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva me hotha, na ca maṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhatha, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākarotha, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati.
segs.e: “Indeed, in answering this way you repeat what I’ve said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Your explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.

segs.p: Dukkhassa hi, bhikkhave, pariññatthaṁ mayi brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: For the goal of leading the spiritual life under me is to completely understand suffering.

segs.p: Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

segs.p: ‘katamaṁ pana taṁ, āvuso, dukkhaṁ, yassa pariññāya samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Reverends, what is that suffering?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: You should answer them:

segs.p: ‘cakkhu kho, āvuso, dukkhaṁ, tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: ‘Reverends, the eye is suffering. The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.
Sights … Eye consciousness … Eye contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.
Ear … Nose … Tongue … Body … Mind …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho taṁ, āvuso, dukkhaṁ, tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti.
segs.e: This is that suffering. The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”

8. Sick
A Question On the World

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘the world’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, lokoti vuccatī”ti?
segs.e: How is the world defined?”
“It wears away, mendicant, that’s why it’s called ‘the world’.
And what is wearing away?
The eye is wearing away.

segs.p: Rūpā lujjanti, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ lujjati, cakkhusamphasso lujjati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi lujjati …pe…
segs.e: Sights … eye consciousness … eye contact is wearing away. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also wearing away.
The ear … nose … tongue … body ….

segs.p: mano lujjati, dhammā lujjanti, manoviññāṇaṁ lujjati, manosamphasso lujjati, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi lujjati.
segs.e: The mind … ideas … mind consciousness … mind contact is wearing away. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also wearing away.

segs.p: Lujjatīti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā lokoti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: It wears away, mendicant, that’s why it’s called ‘the world’.”

8. Sick
Phagguna’s Question

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā phagguno …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā phagguno bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Venerable Phagguna went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

segs.p: “Atthi nu kho, bhante, taṁ cakkhu, yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya …pe…
segs.e: “Sir, suppose someone were to describe the Buddhas of the past who have become fully quenched, cut off proliferation, cut off the course, finished off the cycle, and passed beyond all suffering. Does the eye exist by which they could be described?

segs.p: atthi nu kho, bhante, sā jivhā, yāya jivhāya atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya …pe…
segs.e: Does the ear … nose … tongue … body exist …?

segs.p: atthi nu kho so, bhante, mano, yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Does the mind exist by which they could be described?”

segs.p: “Natthi kho taṁ, phagguna, cakkhu, yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya …pe…
segs.e: “Phagguna, suppose someone were to describe the Buddhas of the past who have become fully quenched, cut off proliferation, cut off the course, finished off the cycle, and passed beyond all suffering. The eye does not exist by which they could be described.

segs.p: natthi kho sā, phagguna, jivhā, yāya jivhāya atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya …pe…
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body does not exist ….

segs.p: natthi kho so, phagguna, mano, yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti.
segs.e: The mind does not exist by which they could be described.”
Linked Discourses 35.84
9. With Channa
Liable to Wear Out
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘the world’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, lokoti vuccatī”ti?
segs.e: How is the world defined?”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṁ, ayaṁ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko.
segs.e: “Ānanda, that which is liable to wear out is called the world in the training of the Noble One.
And what is liable to wear out?

segs.p: Cakkhu kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṁ, rūpā palokadhammā, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ palokadhammaṁ, cakkhusamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā …pe… tampi palokadhammaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The eye is liable to wear out. Sights … eye consciousness … eye contact is liable to wear out. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also liable to wear out.

segs.p: jivhā palokadhammā, rasā palokadhammā, jivhāviññāṇaṁ palokadhammaṁ, jivhāsamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā …pe… tampi palokadhammaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body ….

segs.p: mano palokadhammo, dhammā palokadhammā, manoviññāṇaṁ palokadhammaṁ, manosamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi palokadhammaṁ.
segs.e: The mind … ideas … mind consciousness … mind contact is liable to wear out. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also liable to wear out.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṁ, ayaṁ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko”ti.
segs.e: That which is liable to wear out is called the world in the training of the Noble One.”
Linked Discourses 35.85
9. With Channa
The World is Empty

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando …pe… bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Venerable Ānanda … said to the Buddha:
“Sir, they say that ‘the world is empty’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, suñño lokoti vuccatī”ti?
segs.e: What does the saying ‘the world is empty’ refer to?”

segs.p: “Yasmā ca kho, ānanda, suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā tasmā suñño lokoti vuccati.
segs.e: “Ānanda, they say that ‘the world is empty’ because it’s empty of self or what belongs to self.

segs.p: Kiñca, ānanda, suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā?
segs.e: And what is empty of self or what belongs to self?

segs.p: Cakkhu kho, ānanda, suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā.
segs.e: The eye,

segs.p: Rūpā suññā attena vā attaniyena vā, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā, cakkhusamphasso suñño attena vā attaniyena vā …pe…
segs.e: sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact are empty of self or what belongs to self. …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā.
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also empty of self or what belongs to self.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, ānanda, suññaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā, tasmā suñño lokoti vuccatī”ti.
segs.e: They say that ‘the world is empty’ because it’s empty of self or what belongs to self.”
Linked Discourses 35.86
9. With Channa
A Teaching In Brief

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”
“What do you think, Ānanda?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Are sights …
eye consciousness … eye contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.” …
“Is the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, ānanda, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati …pe… cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
Linked Discourses 35.87
9. With Channa
With Channa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmā ca channo gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti.
segs.e: Now at that time the venerables Sāriputta, Mahācunda, and Channa were staying on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena yena āyasmā channo ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Channa was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahācundo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahācundaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Mahācunda and said to him,
“Come, Reverend Cunda, let’s go to see Venerable Channa and ask about his illness.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā mahācundo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” replied Mahācunda.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo yenāyasmā channo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṁsu. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ channaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Sāriputta and Mahācunda went to see Channa and sat down on the seats spread out. Sāriputta said to Channa:

segs.p: “kacci te, āvuso channa, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, Reverend Channa, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya; evameva kho, āvuso, adhimattā vātā muddhani ūhananti.
segs.e: The winds piercing my head are so severe, it feels like a strong man drilling into my head with a sharp point.

segs.p: Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ …pe… no paṭikkamo.
Seyyathāpi, āvuso, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīse sīsaveṭhaṁ dadeyya; evameva kho, āvuso, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā.
segs.e: The pain in my head is so severe, it feels like a strong man tightening a strong leather strap around my head.

segs.p: Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ …pe… no paṭikkamo.
Seyyathāpi, āvuso, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṁ parikanteyya; evameva kho adhimattā vātā kucchiṁ parikantanti.
segs.e: The winds slicing my belly are so severe, like a deft butcher or their apprentice were slicing open a cow’s belly with a sharp meat cleaver.

segs.p: Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ …pe… no paṭikkamo.
Seyyathāpi, āvuso, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṁ purisaṁ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṁ samparitāpeyyuṁ; evameva kho, āvuso, adhimatto kāyasmiṁ ḍāho.
segs.e: The burning in my body is so severe, it feels like two strong men grabbing a weaker man by the arms to burn and scorch him on a pit of glowing coals.

segs.p: Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

segs.p: Satthaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, āharissāmi, nāvakaṅkhāmi jīvitan”ti.
segs.e: Reverend Sāriputta, I shall commit suicide. I don’t wish to live.”
“Please don’t commit suicide!

segs.p: Yāpetāyasmā channo, yāpentaṁ mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ channaṁ icchāma.
segs.e: Venerable Channa, keep going! We want you to keep going.

segs.p: Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni, ahaṁ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhojanāni pariyesissāmi.
segs.e: If you don’t have any suitable food, we’ll find it for you.

segs.p: Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhesajjāni, ahaṁ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhesajjāni pariyesissāmi.
segs.e: If you don’t have suitable medicine, we’ll find it for you.

segs.p: Sace āyasmato channassa natthi patirūpā upaṭṭhākā, ahaṁ āyasmantaṁ channaṁ upaṭṭhahissāmi.
segs.e: If you don’t have a capable carer, we’ll find one for you.
Please don’t commit suicide!

segs.p: Yāpetāyasmā channo, yāpentaṁ mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ channaṁ icchāmā”ti.
segs.e: Venerable Channa, keep going! We want you to keep going.”

segs.p: “Na me, āvuso sāriputta, natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni;
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, it’s not that I don’t have suitable food;
I do have suitable food.
It’s not that I don’t have suitable medicine;
I do have suitable medicine.
It’s not that I don’t have a capable carer;
I do have a capable carer.

segs.p: Api ca me, āvuso, satthā pariciṇṇo dīgharattaṁ manāpeneva, no amanāpena.
segs.e: Moreover, for a long time now I have served the Teacher with love, not without love.

segs.p: Etañhi, āvuso, sāvakassa patirūpaṁ yaṁ satthāraṁ paricareyya manāpeneva, no amanāpena.
segs.e: For it is proper for a disciple to serve the Teacher with love, not without love.

segs.p: ‘Anupavajjaṁ channo bhikkhu satthaṁ āharissatī’ti—evametaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, dhārehī”ti.
segs.e: You should remember this: ‘The mendicant Channa will commit suicide blamelessly.’”

segs.p: “Puccheyyāma mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ channaṁ kañcideva desaṁ, sace āyasmā channo okāsaṁ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti.
segs.e: “I’d like to ask Venerable Channa about a certain point, if you’d take the time to answer.”
“Ask, Reverend Sāriputta. When I’ve heard it I’ll know.”

segs.p: “Cakkhuṁ, āvuso channa, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasi …pe…
segs.e: “Reverend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye consciousness, and things knowable by eye consciousness in this way: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?

segs.p: jivhaṁ, āvuso channa, jivhāviññāṇaṁ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasi …pe…
segs.e: Do you regard the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manaṁ, āvuso channa, manoviññāṇaṁ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?
segs.e: mind, mind consciousness, and things knowable by mind consciousness in this way: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

segs.p: “Cakkhuṁ, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi …pe…
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, I regard the eye, eye consciousness, and things knowable by eye consciousness in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: jivhaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, jivhāviññāṇaṁ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi …pe…
segs.e: I regard the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, manoviññāṇaṁ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmī”ti.
segs.e: mind, mind consciousness, and things knowable by mind consciousness in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’.”

segs.p: “Cakkhusmiṁ, āvuso channa, cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṁ disvā kiṁ abhiññāya cakkhuṁ cakkhuviññāṇaṁ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasi …
segs.e: “Reverend Channa, what have you seen, what have you directly known in these things that you regard them in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’?”

segs.p: jivhāya, āvuso channa, jivhāviññāṇe jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṁ disvā kiṁ abhiññāya jivhaṁ jivhāviññāṇaṁ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasi …

manasmiṁ, āvuso channa, manoviññāṇe manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṁ disvā kiṁ abhiññāya manaṁ manoviññāṇaṁ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?

“Cakkhusmiṁ, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṁ disvā nirodhaṁ abhiññāya cakkhuṁ cakkhuviññāṇaṁ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi …pe…
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, after seeing cessation, after directly knowing cessation in these things I regard them in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’.”

segs.p: jivhāya, āvuso sāriputta, jivhāviññāṇe jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṁ disvā nirodhaṁ abhiññāya jivhaṁ jivhāviññāṇaṁ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi …pe…

manasmiṁ, āvuso sāriputta, manoviññāṇe manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṁ disvā nirodhaṁ abhiññāya manaṁ manoviññāṇaṁ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā mahācundo āyasmantaṁ channaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Mahācunda said to Venerable Channa,

segs.p: “tasmātiha, āvuso channa, idampi tassa bhagavato sāsanaṁ niccakappaṁ sādhukaṁ manasi kātabbaṁ:
segs.e: “So, Reverend Channa, you should regularly apply your mind well to this instruction of the Buddha:
‘For the dependent there is quivering. For the independent there’s no quivering.
When there’s no quivering, there is tranquility.
When there is tranquility, there’s no inclination.
When there’s no inclination, there’s no coming and going.
When there’s no coming and going, there’s no passing away and reappearing.

segs.p: Cutūpapāte asati nevidha na huraṁ na ubhayamantarena.
segs.e: When there’s no passing away and reappearing, there’s no this life or the next or between the two.
Just this is the end of suffering.’”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmantaṁ channaṁ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṁsu.
segs.e: And when the venerables Sāriputta and Mahācunda had given Venerable Channa this advice they rose from their seats and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā channo acirapakkantesu tesu āyasmantesu satthaṁ āharesi.
segs.e: Not long after those venerables had left, Venerable Channa committed suicide.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, Venerable Channa has committed suicide.
Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

segs.p: “Nanu te, sāriputta, channena bhikkhunā sammukhāyeva anupavajjatā byākatā”ti?
segs.e: “Sāriputta, didn’t the mendicant Channa declare his blamelessness to you personally?”
“Sir, there is a Vajjian village named Pubbajira.
There Channa had families who were friendly, intimate, and hospitable.”

segs.p: “Honti hete, sāriputta, channassa bhikkhuno mittakulāni suhajjakulāni upavajjakulāni.
segs.e: “The mendicant Channa did indeed have such families.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ, sāriputta, ettāvatā saupavajjoti vadāmi.
segs.e: But, Sāriputta, this is not enough for me to call someone ‘blameworthy’.

segs.p: Yo kho, sāriputta, tañca kāyaṁ nikkhipati, aññañca kāyaṁ upādiyati, tamahaṁ saupavajjoti vadāmi.
segs.e: When someone lays down this body and takes up another body, I call them ‘blameworthy’.
But the mendicant Channa did no such thing.
You should remember this: ‘The mendicant Channa committed suicide blamelessly.’”

9. With Channa
With Puṇṇa

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā puṇṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Venerable Puṇṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Santi kho, puṇṇa, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Puṇṇa, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, puṇṇa, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
segs.e: this gives rise to relishing.
Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.

segs.p: Santi kho, puṇṇa, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nirujjhati nandī.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.
When relishing ceases, suffering ceases, I say. …

segs.p: santi kho, puṇṇa, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nirujjhati nandī.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.
When relishing ceases, suffering ceases, I say.

segs.p: Iminā tvaṁ, puṇṇa, mayā saṅkhittena ovādena ovadito katamasmiṁ janapade viharissasī”ti?
segs.e: Puṇṇa, now that I’ve given you this brief advice, what country will you live in?”

segs.p: “Atthi, bhante, sunāparanto nāma janapado, tatthāhaṁ viharissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, there’s a country named Sunāparanta; I will live there.”
“The people of Sunāparanta are wild and rough, Puṇṇa.

segs.p: Sace taṁ, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā akkosissanti paribhāsissanti, tatra te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: If they abuse and insult you, what will you think of them?”

segs.p: “Sace maṁ, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā akkosissanti paribhāsissanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they abuse and insult me, I will think:

segs.p: ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṁ me nayime pāṇinā pahāraṁ dentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘These people of Sunāparanta are gracious, truly gracious, since they don’t hit me with their fists.’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”

segs.p: “Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā pāṇinā pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they do hit you with their fists, what will you think of them then?”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā pāṇinā pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they hit me with their fists, I’ll think:

segs.p: ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṁ me nayime leḍḍunā pahāraṁ dentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘These people of Sunāparanta are gracious, truly gracious, since they don’t throw stones at me.’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”

segs.p: “Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā leḍḍunā pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they do throw stones at you, what will you think of them then?”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā leḍḍunā pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they throw stones at me, I’ll think:

segs.p: ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṁ me nayime daṇḍena pahāraṁ dentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘These people of Sunāparanta are gracious, truly gracious, since they don’t beat me with a club.’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”

segs.p: “Sace pana puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā daṇḍena pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they do beat you with a club, what will you think of them then?”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā daṇḍena pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they beat me with a club, I’ll think:

segs.p: ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṁ me nayime satthena pahāraṁ dentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘These people of Sunāparanta are gracious, truly gracious, since they don’t stab me with a knife.’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”

segs.p: “Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā satthena pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they do stab you with a knife, what will you think of them then?”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā satthena pahāraṁ dassanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they stab me with a knife, I’ll think:

segs.p: ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṁ maṁ nayime tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘These people of Sunāparanta are gracious, truly gracious, since they don’t take my life with a sharp knife.’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”

segs.p: “Sace pana taṁ, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropessanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “But if they do take your life with a sharp knife, what will you think of them then?”

segs.p: “Sace maṁ, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropessanti, tatra me evaṁ bhavissati:
segs.e: “If they take my life with a sharp knife, I’ll think:

segs.p: ‘santi kho tassa bhagavato sāvakā kāyena ca jīvitena ca aṭṭīyamānā harāyamānā jigucchamānā satthahārakaṁ pariyesanti, taṁ me idaṁ apariyiṭṭhaññeva satthahārakaṁ laddhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘There are disciples of the Buddha who looked for a suicide weapon because they were horrified, repelled, and disgusted with the body and with life. And I have found this without looking!’
That’s what I’ll think, Blessed One.
That’s what I’ll think, Holy One.”
“Good, good Puṇṇa!

segs.p: Sakkhissasi kho tvaṁ, puṇṇa, iminā damūpasamena samannāgato sunāparantasmiṁ janapade vatthuṁ.
segs.e: Having such self-control and peacefulness, you will be quite capable of living in Sunāparanta.
Now, Puṇṇa, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo bhagavato vacanaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā senāsanaṁ saṁsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sunāparanto janapado tena cārikaṁ pakkāmi.
segs.e: And then Puṇṇa welcomed and agreed with the Buddha’s words. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, set out for Sunāparanta.

segs.p: Anupubbena cārikaṁ caramāno yena sunāparanto janapado tadavasari.
segs.e: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sunāparanta,

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ āyasmā puṇṇo sunāparantasmiṁ janapade viharati.
segs.e: and stayed there.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo tenevantaravassena pañcamattāni upāsakasatāni paṭivedesi.
segs.e: Within that rainy season he confirmed around five hundred male and five hundred female lay followers. And within that same rainy season he realized the three knowledges.
And within that same rainy season he became fully extinguished.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “yo so, bhante, puṇṇo nāma kulaputto bhagavatā saṅkhittena ovādena ovadito, so kālaṅkato.
segs.e: “Sir, the gentleman named Puṇṇa, who was advised in brief by the Buddha, has passed away.
Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

segs.p: “Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, puṇṇo kulaputto, paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṁ, na ca maṁ dhammādhikaraṇaṁ vihesesi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, Puṇṇa was astute. He practiced in line with the teaching, and did not trouble me about the teachings.
Puṇṇa has become completely quenched.”
Linked Discourses 35.89
9. With Channa
With Bāhiya

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Bāhiya went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”
“What do you think, Bāhiya?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Are sights …
eye consciousness …
eye contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bāhiya, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And then Venerable Bāhiya approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Bāhiya, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā bāhiyo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Bāhiya became one of the perfected.
Linked Discourses 35.90
9. With Channa
Turbulence (1st)

segs.p: “Ejā, bhikkhave, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, turbulence is a disease, a boil, a dart.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tathāgato anejo viharati vītasallo.
segs.e: That’s why the Realized One lives unperturbed, with dart drawn out.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cepi ākaṅkheyya ‘anejo vihareyyaṁ vītasallo’ti,
segs.e: Now, a mendicant might wish: ‘May I live unperturbed, with dart drawn out.’

segs.p: cakkhuṁ na maññeyya, cakkhusmiṁ na maññeyya, cakkhuto na maññeyya, cakkhu meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: So let them not conceive anything to be the eye, let them not conceive it in the eye, let them not conceive it as the eye, let them not conceive that ‘the eye is mine.’

segs.p: rūpe na maññeyya, rūpesu na maññeyya, rūpato na maññeyya, rūpā meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: Let them not conceive sights …

segs.p: cakkhuviññāṇaṁ na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇasmiṁ na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇato na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: eye consciousness …

segs.p: cakkhusamphassaṁ na maññeyya, cakkhusamphassasmiṁ na maññeyya, cakkhusamphassato na maññeyya, cakkhusamphasso meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: eye contact …

segs.p: Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact. Let them not conceive it in that, let them not conceive it as that, and let them not conceive that ‘that is mine.’
Let them not conceive anything to be the ear …
nose …

segs.p: jivhaṁ na maññeyya, jivhāya na maññeyya, jivhāto na maññeyya, jivhā meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: tongue …

segs.p: yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.

segs.e: body …

segs.p: manaṁ na maññeyya, manasmiṁ na maññeyya, manato na maññeyya, mano meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: mind …
ideas …
mind consciousness …
mind contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact. Let them not conceive it in that, let them not conceive it as that, and let them not conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: sabbaṁ na maññeyya, sabbasmiṁ na maññeyya, sabbato na maññeyya, sabbaṁ meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be all, let them not conceive it in all, let them not conceive it as all, let them not conceive that ‘all is mine’.

segs.p: So evaṁ amaññamāno na kiñcipi loke upādiyati.
segs.e: Not conceiving, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

segs.p: Anupādiyaṁ na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

9. With Channa
Turbulence (2nd)

segs.p: “Ejā, bhikkhave, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, turbulence is a disease, a boil, a dart.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tathāgato anejo viharati vītasallo.
segs.e: That’s why the Realized One lives unperturbed, with dart drawn out.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cepi ākaṅkheyya ‘anejo vihareyyaṁ vītasallo’ti,
segs.e: Now, a mendicant might wish: ‘May I live unperturbed, with dart drawn out.’

segs.p: cakkhuṁ na maññeyya, cakkhusmiṁ na maññeyya, cakkhuto na maññeyya, cakkhu meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: So let them not conceive anything to be the eye, let them not conceive it in the eye, let them not conceive it as the eye, let them not conceive that ‘the eye is mine.’
Let them not conceive sights …
eye consciousness …
eye contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact. Let them not conceive it in that, let them not conceive it as that, and let them not conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṁ maññati, yato maññati, yaṁ meti maññati, tato taṁ hoti aññathā.
segs.e: For whatever you conceive it to be, whatever you conceive it in, whatever you conceive it as, and whatever you conceive to be ‘mine’: that becomes something else.
The world is attached to being, taking pleasure only in being, yet it becomes something else.

segs.p: Jivhaṁ na maññeyya, jivhāya na maññeyya, jivhāto na maññeyya, jivhā meti na maññeyya;
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.
Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṁ maññati, yato maññati, yaṁ meti maññati, tato taṁ hoti aññathā. Aññathābhāvī bhavasatto loko bhavameva abhinandati …pe….
Manaṁ na maññeyya, manasmiṁ na maññeyya, manato na maññeyya, mano meti na maññeyya …
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the mind …
mind consciousness …
mind contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: Let them not conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact. Let them not conceive it in that, let them not conceive it as that, and let them not conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṁ maññati, yato maññati, yaṁ meti maññati, tato taṁ hoti aññathā.
segs.e: For whatever you conceive it to be, whatever you conceive it in, whatever you conceive it as, and whatever you conceive to be ‘mine’: that becomes something else.
The world is attached to being, taking pleasure only in being, yet it becomes something else.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bhikkhave, khandhadhātuāyatanā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṁ meti na maññeyya.
segs.e: As far as the aggregates, elements, and sense fields extend, they don’t conceive anything to be that, they don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

segs.p: So evaṁ amaññamāno na kiñci loke upādiyati.
segs.e: Not conceiving, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

segs.p: Anupādiyaṁ na paritassati. Aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
Linked Discourses 35.92
9. With Channa
A Duality (1st)
“Mendicants, I will teach you a duality.
Listen …
And what is a duality?

segs.p: Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañceva saddā ca, ghānañceva gandhā ca, jivhā ceva rasā ca, kāyo ceva phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ceva dhammā ca—
segs.e: It’s just the eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.
This is called a duality.
Mendicants, suppose someone was to say:

segs.p: ‘ahametaṁ dvayaṁ paccakkhāya aññaṁ dvayaṁ paññapessāmī’ti, tassa vācāvatthukamevassa.
segs.e: ‘I’ll deny this duality and describe another duality.’ They’d have no grounds for that claim,
they’d be stumped by questions, and, in addition, they’d get frustrated.
Why is that?
Because they’re out of their element.”
Linked Discourses 35.93
9. With Channa
A Duality (2nd)
“Mendicants, consciousness originates dependent on a duality.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, dvayaṁ paṭicca viññāṇaṁ sambhoti?
segs.e: And what is that duality?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights.
The eye is impermanent, decaying, and perishing.
Sights are impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Itthetaṁ dvayaṁ calañceva byathañca aniccaṁ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi.
segs.e: So this duality is tottering and toppling; it’s impermanent, decaying, and perishing.
Eye consciousness is impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Yopi hetu yopi paccayo cakkhuviññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
segs.e: And the causes and reasons that give rise to eye consciousness are also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppannaṁ cakkhuviññāṇaṁ kuto niccaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: But since eye consciousness has arisen dependent on conditions that are impermanent, how could it be permanent?

segs.p: Yā kho, bhikkhave, imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ saṅgati sannipāto samavāyo, ayaṁ vuccati cakkhusamphasso.
segs.e: The meeting, coming together, and joining together of these three things is called eye contact.
Eye contact is also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Yopi hetu yopi paccayo cakkhusamphassassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
segs.e: And the causes and reasons that give rise to eye contact are also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppanno cakkhusamphasso kuto nicco bhavissati.
segs.e: But since eye contact has arisen dependent on conditions that are impermanent, how could it be permanent?

segs.p: Phuṭṭho, bhikkhave, vedeti, phuṭṭho ceteti, phuṭṭho sañjānāti.
segs.e: Contacted one feels; contacted one intends; contacted one perceives.

segs.p: Itthetepi dhammā calā ceva byathā ca aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino …pe…
segs.e: So these things too are tottering and toppling; they’re impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Ear consciousness … Nose consciousness … Tongue consciousness … Body consciousness …

segs.p: Itthetaṁ dvayaṁ calañceva byathañca aniccaṁ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi.
Yopi hetu yopi paccayo jivhāviññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppannaṁ jivhāviññāṇaṁ, kuto niccaṁ bhavissati.
Yā kho, bhikkhave, imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ saṅgati sannipāto samavāyo, ayaṁ vuccati jivhāsamphasso.
Yopi hetu yopi paccayo jivhāsamphassassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppanno jivhāsamphasso, kuto nicco bhavissati.
Phuṭṭho, bhikkhave, vedeti, phuṭṭho ceteti, phuṭṭho sañjānāti.
Itthetepi dhammā calā ceva byathā ca aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino …pe…
Manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas.
The mind is impermanent, decaying, and perishing.
Ideas are impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Itthetaṁ dvayaṁ calañceva byathañca aniccaṁ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi.
segs.e: So this duality is tottering and toppling; it’s impermanent, decaying, and perishing.
Mind consciousness is impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Yopi hetu yopi paccayo manoviññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
segs.e: And the causes and reasons that give rise to mind consciousness are also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppannaṁ manoviññāṇaṁ, kuto niccaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: But since mind consciousness has arisen dependent on conditions that are impermanent, how could it be permanent?

segs.p: Yā kho, bhikkhave, imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ saṅgati sannipāto samavāyo, ayaṁ vuccati manosamphasso.
segs.e: The meeting, coming together, and joining together of these three things is called mind contact.
Mind contact is also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Yopi hetu yopi paccayo manosamphassassa uppādāya, sopi hetu sopi paccayo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī.
segs.e: And the causes and reasons that give rise to mind contact are also impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Aniccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, paccayaṁ paṭicca uppanno manosamphasso, kuto nicco bhavissati.
segs.e: But since mind contact has arisen dependent on conditions that are impermanent, how could it be permanent?

segs.p: Phuṭṭho, bhikkhave, vedeti, phuṭṭho ceteti, phuṭṭho sañjānāti.
segs.e: Contacted one feels; contacted one intends; contacted one perceives.

segs.p: Itthetepi dhammā calā ceva byathā ca aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino.
segs.e: So these things too are tottering and toppling; they’re impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvayaṁ paṭicca viññāṇaṁ sambhotī”ti.
segs.e: This is how consciousness originates dependent on a duality.”
Linked Discourses 35.94
10. The Sixes
Untamed, Unguarded
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, phassāyatanā adantā aguttā arakkhitā asaṁvutā dukkhādhivāhā honti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six fields of contact bring suffering when they’re untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.
What six?

segs.p: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
segs.e: The field of eye contact brings suffering when it’s untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

segs.p: jivhā, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
segs.e: The field of ear contact … nose contact … tongue contact … body contact …

segs.p: mano, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ dukkhādhivāhaṁ hoti.
segs.e: The field of mind contact brings suffering when it’s untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanā adantā aguttā arakkhitā asaṁvutā dukkhādhivāhā honti”.
segs.e: These six fields of contact bring suffering when they’re untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained.

segs.p: Chayime, bhikkhave, phassāyatanā sudantā suguttā surakkhitā susaṁvutā sukhādhivāhā honti.
segs.e: These six fields of contact bring happiness when they’re well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.
What six?

segs.p: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
segs.e: The field of eye contact brings happiness when it’s well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.

segs.p: jivhā, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti …pe…
segs.e: The field of ear contact … nose contact … tongue contact … body contact …

segs.p: mano, bhikkhave, phassāyatanaṁ sudantaṁ suguttaṁ surakkhitaṁ susaṁvutaṁ sukhādhivāhaṁ hoti.
segs.e: The field of mind contact brings happiness when it’s well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanā sudantā suguttā surakkhitā susaṁvutā sukhādhivāhā hontī”ti.
segs.e: These six fields of contact bring happiness when they’re well tamed, well guarded, well protected, and well restrained.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Mendicants, it’s just the six fields of contact
that lead the unrestrained to suffering.
Those who understand how to restrain them
live with faith as partner, not festering.
When you’ve seen pleasant sights
and unpleasant ones, too,
dispel all manner of desire for the pleasant,
without hating what you don’t like.
When you’ve heard sounds both liked and disliked,
don’t fall under the thrall of sounds you like,
dispel hate for the unliked,
and don’t hurt your mind <j>by thinking of what you don’t like.
When you’ve smelled a pleasant, fragrant scent,
and one that’s foul and unpleasant,
dispel aversion for the unpleasant,
while not yielding to desire for the pleasant.
When you’ve enjoyed a sweet, delicious taste,
and sometimes those that are bitter,
don’t be attached to enjoying sweet tastes,
and don’t despise the bitter.
Don’t be intoxicated by a pleasant touch,
and don’t tremble at a painful touch.
Look with equanimity at the duality <j>of pleasant and painful contacts,
without favoring or opposing anything.
People generally let their perceptions proliferate;
perceiving and proliferating, they are attracted.
Casting aside all mental constructions <j>of the domestic life,
wander intent on renunciation.
When the mind is well developed like this <j>regarding the six,
it doesn’t waver at contacts at all.
Mendicants, those who have mastered greed and hate
go beyond birth and death.”
Linked Discourses 35.95
10. The Sixes
Māluṅkyaputta

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Māluṅkyaputta went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Ettha dāni, mālukyaputta, kiṁ dahare bhikkhū vakkhāma.
segs.e: “Well now, Māluṅkyaputta, what are we to say to the young monks,

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma tvaṁ, bhikkhu, jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto saṅkhittena ovādaṁ yācasī”ti.
segs.e: when even an old man like you, elderly and senior, advanced in years, having reached the final stage of life, asks for brief advice?”

segs.p: “Kiñcāpāhaṁ, bhante, jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto.
segs.e: “Sir, even though I’m an old man, elderly and senior,

segs.p: Desetu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ, desetu sugato saṅkhittena dhammaṁ, appeva nāmāhaṁ bhagavato bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājāneyyaṁ. Appeva nāmāhaṁ bhagavato bhāsitassa dāyādo assan”ti.
segs.e: may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief! May the Holy One please teach me in brief! Hopefully I can understand the meaning of what the Buddha says. Hopefully I can be an heir of the Buddha’s teaching!”
“What do you think, Māluṅkyaputta?

segs.p: ye te cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā adiṭṭhā adiṭṭhapubbā, na ca passasi, na ca te hoti passeyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: Do you have any desire or greed or fondness for sights known by the eye that are unseen, unseen before, and which you neither see nor think might be seen?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ye te sotaviññeyyā saddā assutā assutapubbā, na ca suṇāsi, na ca te hoti suṇeyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “Do you have any desire or greed or affection for sounds known by the ear …

segs.p: “Ye te ghānaviññeyyā gandhā aghāyitā aghāyitapubbā, na ca ghāyasi, na ca te hoti ghāyeyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: smells known by the nose …

segs.p: “Ye te jivhāviññeyyā rasā asāyitā asāyitapubbā, na ca sāyasi, na ca te hoti sāyeyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: “Ye te kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā asamphuṭṭhā asamphuṭṭhapubbā, na ca phusasi, na ca te hoti phuseyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: touches known by the body …

segs.p: “Ye te manoviññeyyā dhammā aviññātā aviññātapubbā, na ca vijānāsi, na ca te hoti vijāneyyanti? Atthi te tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: ideas known by the mind that are unknown, unknown before, and which you neither know nor think might be known?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ettha ca te, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhasutamutaviññātabbesu dhammesu diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṁ bhavissati, sute sutamattaṁ bhavissati, mute mutamattaṁ bhavissati, viññāte viññātamattaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: “In that case, when it comes to things that ought be seen, heard, thought, and known: in the seen will be merely the seen; in the heard will be merely the heard; in the thought will be merely the thought; in the known will be merely the known.

segs.p: Yato kho te, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhasutamutaviññātabbesu dhammesu diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṁ bhavissati, sute sutamattaṁ bhavissati, mute mutamattaṁ bhavissati, viññāte viññātamattaṁ bhavissati;
segs.e: When this is the case,
you won’t be ‘by that’.
When you’re not ‘by that’,
you won’t be ‘in that’.
When you’re not ‘in that’,

segs.p: tato tvaṁ, mālukyaputta, nevidha, na huraṁ, na ubhayamantarena.
segs.e: you won’t be in this life or the next or in between the two.
Just this is the end of suffering.”

segs.p: “Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi:
segs.e: “This is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement:
‘When you see a sight, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from sights.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
When you hear a sound, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from sounds.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
When you smell an odor, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from smells.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
When you enjoy a taste, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from tastes.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
When you sense a touch, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from touches.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
When you know an idea, mindfulness is lost
as you focus on a pleasant feature.
Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,
you keep clinging to it.
Many feelings grow
arising from ideas.
The mind is damaged
by covetousness and cruelty.
Heaping up suffering like this,
you’re said to be far from extinguishment.
There’s no desire for sights
when you see a sight with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you see a sight
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.
There’s no desire for sounds
when you hear a sound with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you hear a sound
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.
There’s no desire for odors
when you smell an odor with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you smell an odor
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.
There’s no desire for tastes
when you enjoy a taste with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you savor a taste
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.
There’s no desire for touches
when you sense a touch with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you sense a touch
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.
There’s no desire for ideas
when you know an idea with mindfulness.
Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,
you don’t keep clinging to it.
Even as you know an idea
and get familiar with how it feels,
you wear away, you don’t heap up:
that’s how to live mindfully.
Eroding suffering like this,
you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.’

segs.p: Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”
“Good, good, Māluṅkyaputta!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, mālukyaputta, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi:
segs.e: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.” And he repeated the verses in full.

segs.p: Imassa kho, mālukyaputta, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
segs.e: “This is how to see the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And then Venerable Māluṅkyaputta approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Māluṅkyaputta, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā mālukyaputto arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Māluṅkyaputta became one of the perfected.

10. The Sixes
Liable to Decline

segs.p: “Parihānadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi aparihānadhammañca cha ca abhibhāyatanāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you who is liable to decline, who is not liable to decline, and the six fields of mastery.
Listen …
And how is someone liable to decline?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu adhivāseti nappajahati na vinodeti na byantīkaroti na anabhāvaṁ gameti, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: Suppose that mendicant tolerates them and doesn’t give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them. They should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā uppajjanti …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … encounters a touch …

segs.p: puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu adhivāseti nappajahati na vinodeti na byantīkaroti na anabhāvaṁ gameti, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: If that mendicant tolerates them and doesn’t give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them, they should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’
That’s how someone is liable to decline.
And how is someone not liable to decline?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: Suppose that mendicant doesn’t tolerate them but gives them up, dispels them, eliminates them, and obliterates them. They should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā uppajjanti …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … encounters a touch …

segs.p: puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: Suppose that mendicant doesn’t tolerate them but gives them up, dispels them, eliminates them, and obliterates them. They should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’
That’s how someone is not liable to decline.
And what are the six fields of mastery?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā nuppajjanti pāpakā akusalā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, bad, unskillful phenomena don’t arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.
They should understand:
‘This sense field has been mastered.
For this is what the Buddha calls a field of mastery.’ …

segs.p: puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya nuppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when a mendicant knows an idea with their mind, bad, unskillful phenomena don’t arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.
They should understand:
‘This sense field has been mastered.
For this is what the Buddha calls a field of mastery.’
These are the six fields of mastery.”

10. The Sixes
One Who Lives Negligently
“Mendicants, I will teach you who lives negligently and who lives diligently.
Listen …
And how does someone live negligently?

segs.p: Cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ byāsiñcati cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu.
segs.e: When you live with the eye faculty unrestrained, your mind becomes polluted when it comes to sights known by the eye.
When the mind is polluted, there’s no joy.
When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.
When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.
When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.
When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.
Because principles have not become clear, you’re reckoned to live negligently.

segs.p: jivhindriyaṁ asaṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ byāsiñcati jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu,
segs.e: When you live with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manindriyaṁ asaṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ byāsiñcati manoviññeyyesu dhammesu,
segs.e: mind faculty unrestrained, your mind becomes polluted when it comes to ideas known by the mind.
When the mind is polluted, there’s no joy.
When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.
When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.
When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.
When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.
Because principles have not become clear, you’re reckoned to live negligently.
That’s how someone lives negligently.
And how does someone live diligently?

segs.p: Cakkhundriyaṁ saṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ na byāsiñcati cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu,
segs.e: When you live with the eye faculty restrained, your mind doesn’t become polluted when it comes to sights known by the eye.
When the mind isn’t polluted, joy springs up.
Being joyful, rapture springs up.
When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.
Because principles have become clear, you’re reckoned to live diligently.

segs.p: jivhindriyaṁ saṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ na byāsiñcati …pe…
segs.e: When you live with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Manindriyaṁ saṁvutassa, bhikkhave, viharato cittaṁ na byāsiñcati, manoviññeyyesu dhammesu,
segs.e: mind faculty restrained, your mind doesn’t become polluted when it comes to ideas known by the mind.
When the mind isn’t polluted, joy springs up.
Being joyful, rapture springs up.
When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.
Because principles have become clear, you’re reckoned to live diligently.
That’s how someone lives diligently.”

10. The Sixes
Restraint
“Mendicants, I will teach you who is restrained and who is unrestrained.
Listen …
And how is someone unrestrained?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, they should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, they should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’
This is how someone is unrestrained.
And how is someone restrained?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā:
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, they should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, veditabbametaṁ bhikkhunā:
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, they should understand:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’
This is how someone is restrained.”

segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
And what isn’t yours?
