segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
Sights …

segs.p: Te vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissanti.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.

The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṁ imasmiṁ jetavane tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṁ taṁ jano hareyya vā ḍaheyya vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā kareyya,
segs.e: Suppose a person was to carry off the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves in this Jeta’s Grove, or burn them, or do what they want with them.
Would you think:

segs.p: ‘amhe jano harati vā ḍahati vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karotī’”ti?

“No, sir.
Why is that?

segs.p: “Na hi no etaṁ, bhante, attā vā attaniyaṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: Because  to us that’s neither self nor belonging to self.”
“In the same way, the eye isn’t yours: give it up.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.”

10. The Sixes
About Uddaka

segs.p: “Udako sudaṁ, bhikkhave, rāmaputto evaṁ vācaṁ bhāsati:
segs.e: “Mendicants, Uddaka son of Rāma used to say:
‘Hereupon, ever the knowledge master!
Hereupon, ever the conqueror of all!
Hereupon, ever the undug
boil’s root was dug out by me!’

segs.p: Taṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, udako rāmaputto avedagūyeva samāno ‘vedagūsmī’ti bhāsati, asabbajīyeva samāno ‘sabbajīsmī’ti bhāsati, apalikhataṁyeva gaṇḍamūlaṁ ‘palikhataṁ me gaṇḍamūlan’ti bhāsati.
segs.e: Even though Uddaka son of Rāma was no knowledge master, he said ‘I’m a knowledge master.’ Though he was no conqueror of all, he said ‘I’m conqueror of all.’ And though the boil’s root was not dug out, he said ‘I’ve dug out the boil’s root.’

segs.p: Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: A mendicant might rightly say here:
‘Hereupon, ever the knowledge master!
Hereupon, ever the conqueror of all!
Hereupon, ever the undug
boil’s root is dug out!’
And how is someone a knowledge master?

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedagū hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a knowledge master.
And how is a mendicant a conqueror of all?

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

segs.p: evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbajī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a conqueror of all.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno apalikhataṁ gaṇḍamūlaṁ palikhataṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how has a mendicant dug out the undug boil’s root?

segs.p: Gaṇḍoti kho, bhikkhave, imassetaṁ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṁ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammassa.
segs.e: ‘Boil’ is a term for this body made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.
‘Boil’s root’ is a term for craving.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has given up craving, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno apalikhataṁ gaṇḍamūlaṁ palikhataṁ hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has dug out the undug boil’s root.

segs.p: Udako sudaṁ, bhikkhave, rāmaputto evaṁ vācaṁ bhāsati:
segs.e: Uddaka son of Rāma used to say:
‘Hereupon, ever the knowledge master!
Hereupon, ever the conqueror of all!
Hereupon, ever the undug
boil’s root is dug out!’

segs.p: Taṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, udako rāmaputto avedagūyeva samāno ‘vedagūsmī’ti bhāsati, asabbajīyeva samāno ‘sabbajīsmī’ti bhāsati; apalikhataṁyeva gaṇḍamūlaṁ ‘palikhataṁ me gaṇḍamūlan’ti bhāsati.
segs.e: Even though Uddaka son of Rāma was no knowledge master, he said ‘I’m a knowledge master.’ Though he was no conqueror of all, he said ‘I’m conqueror of all.’ And though the boil’s root was not dug out, he said ‘I’ve dug out the boil’s root.’

segs.p: Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: A mendicant might rightly say here:
‘Hereupon, ever the knowledge master!
Hereupon, ever the conqueror of all!
Hereupon, ever the undug
boil’s root is dug out!’”

11. Sanctuary from the Yoke

At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you an exposition of the teaching, an explanation of one who has found sanctuary from the yoke.
Listen …
And what is an exposition of the teaching, an explanation of one who has found sanctuary from the yoke?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Te tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tesañca pahānāya akkhāsi yogaṁ, tasmā tathāgato ‘yogakkhemī’ti vuccati …pe…
segs.e: He teaches yoking oneself to meditation for giving them up. That’s why the Realized One is called one who has found sanctuary from the yoke. …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Te tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One has given these up, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, and obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tesañca pahānāya akkhāsi yogaṁ, tasmā tathāgato ‘yogakkhemī’ti vuccati.
segs.e: He teaches yoking oneself to meditation for giving them up. That’s why the Realized One is called one who has found sanctuary from the yoke.
This is an exposition of the teaching, an explanation of one who has found sanctuary from the yoke.”

11. Sanctuary from the Yoke
The Origin of Suffering
“Mendicants, I will teach you the origin and disappearance of suffering.
Listen …
And what, mendicants, is the origin of suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
This is the origin of suffering …

segs.p: jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
Ayaṁ dukkhassa samudayo …pe… manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas.
The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
This is the origin of suffering.
And what is the disappearance of suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
This is the disappearance of suffering. …

segs.p: jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṁ …pe…

segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.

11. Sanctuary from the Yoke

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā rahogato paṭisallīno imaṁ dhammapariyāyaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then while the Buddha was in private retreat he spoke this exposition of the teaching:

segs.p: “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: “Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
Ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
Ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato upassuti ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain monk was standing listening in on the Buddha.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ upassuti ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him
and said,

memorize it,

segs.p: “Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati—
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṁ gato, paṭimukkassa mārapāso.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati—
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṁ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant not trapped in Māra’s lair, not fallen under Māra’s sway, and released from Māra’s snare.

segs.p: Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato …pe….
segs.e: They’re free from Māra’s bonds, and the Wicked One cannot do with them what he wants.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati—
ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṁ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato …pe….
Santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati—
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṁ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant not trapped in Māra’s lair, not fallen under Māra’s sway, and released from Māra’s snare.

segs.p: Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato”ti.
segs.e: They’re free from Māra’s bonds, and the Wicked One cannot do with them what he wants.”

segs.p: “Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.

segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

Linked Discourses 35.116
12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
Traveling to the End of the World

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling.

segs.p: Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: But I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.”

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
segs.e: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

segs.p: “idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail. …

segs.p: ‘“nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyan”ti vadāmi.
Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī’ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?”
Then those mendicants thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants went to Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

segs.p: “Idaṁ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī’ti.
Tesaṁ no, āvuso, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmīti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho, āvuso, āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.

segs.e: “May Venerable Ānanda please explain this.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṁ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva, mūlaṁ atikkammeva, khandhaṁ sākhāpalāse sāraṁ pariyesitabbaṁ maññeyya;
segs.e: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

segs.p: evaṁ sampadamidaṁ āyasmantānaṁ satthari sammukhībhūte taṁ bhagavantaṁ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṁ paṭipucchitabbaṁ maññatha.
segs.e: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

segs.p: So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passati—
segs.e: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: cakkhubhūto, ñāṇabhūto, dhammabhūto, brahmabhūto, vattā, pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī, tathāgato.
So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ bhagavantaṁyeva etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā vo dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Addhāvuso ānanda, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passati—
segs.e: “Certainly he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: cakkhubhūto, ñāṇabhūto, dhammabhūto, brahmabhūto, vattā, pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī, tathāgato.
So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ bhagavantaṁyeva etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṁ dhāreyyāma.
segs.e: We should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.

segs.p: Api cāyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: Still, Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: You are capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.
Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”
“Then listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: ‘Mendicants, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling.

segs.p: Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī’ti,
segs.e: But I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.’

segs.p: imassa khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: This is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary recital.

segs.p: Yena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī—
segs.e: Whatever in the world through which you perceive the world and conceive the world
is called the world in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Kena cāvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī?
segs.e: And through what in the world do you perceive the world and conceive the world?

segs.p: Cakkhunā kho, āvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī.
segs.e: Through the eye in the world you perceive the world and conceive the world.
Through the ear …
nose …

segs.p: jivhāya kho, āvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī.
segs.e: tongue …
body …

segs.p: manena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī.
segs.e: mind in the world you perceive the world and conceive the world.

segs.p: Yena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṁ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī—
segs.e: Whatever in the world through which you perceive the world and conceive the world
is called the world in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: ‘Mendicants, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling.

segs.p: Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī’ti,
segs.e: But I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.’

segs.p: imassa khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: That is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” replied those mendicants. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmī’ti.
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ, daṭṭheyyaṁ, patteyyanti vadāmi.
Na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmīti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipucchimha.
Tesaṁ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto”ti.
segs.e: Then they said, “And Ānanda explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”
“Mendicants, Ānanda is astute, he has great wisdom.

segs.p: Mañcepi tumhe, bhikkhave, etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi taṁ evamevaṁ byākareyyaṁ yathā taṁ ānandena byākataṁ.
segs.e: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Ānanda.

segs.p: Eso cevetassa attho, evañca naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”
Linked Discourses 35.117
12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
The Kinds of Sensual Stimulation

segs.p: “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘yeme pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra me cittaṁ bahulaṁ gacchamānaṁ gaccheyya paccuppannesu vā appaṁ vā anāgatesu’.
segs.e: ‘My mind might often stray toward the five kinds of sensual stimulation that I formerly experienced—which have passed, ceased, and perished—or to those in the present, or in the future a little.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘yeme pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra me attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo’.
segs.e: ‘In my own way I should practice diligence, mindfulness, and protecting the mind regarding the five kinds of sensual stimulation that I formerly experienced—which have passed, ceased, and perished.’

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhākampi ye te pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra vo cittaṁ bahulaṁ gacchamānaṁ gaccheyya paccuppannesu vā appaṁ vā anāgatesu.
segs.e: So, mendicants, your minds might also often stray toward the five kinds of sensual stimulation that you formerly experienced—which have passed, ceased, and perished—or to those in the present, or in the future a little.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhākampi ye te pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra vo attarūpehi appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo.
segs.e: So in your own way you should practice diligence, mindfulness, and protecting the mind regarding the five kinds of sensual stimulation that you formerly experienced—which have passed, ceased, and perished.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
segs.e: So you should understand that dimension where the eye ceases and perception of sights fades away.

segs.p: yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
segs.e: You should understand that dimension where the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe”ti.
segs.e: mind ceases and perception of ideas fades away.”

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
segs.e: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

segs.p: “idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “The Buddha gave this brief summary, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail. …

segs.p: ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary given by the Buddha?”
Then those mendicants thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary given by the Buddha.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants went to Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

segs.p: “Idaṁ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti.
Tesaṁ no, āvuso, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
“tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe”ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.

segs.e: “May Venerable Ānanda please explain this.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṁ caramāno mahato rukkhassa …pe…
segs.e: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. …”
“Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”
“Then listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

segs.p: ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
segs.e: ‘So you should understand that dimension where the eye ceases and perception of sights fades away. You should understand that dimension where the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti.
segs.e: mind ceases and perception of ideas fades away.’

segs.p: Imassa khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary.

segs.p: Saḷāyatananirodhaṁ no etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: The Buddha was referring to the cessation of the six sense fields when he said:

segs.p: ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe, yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
segs.e: ‘So you should understand that dimension where the eye ceases and perception of sights fades away. You should understand that dimension where the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti.
segs.e: mind ceases and perception of ideas fades away.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: The Buddha gave this brief summary, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail.

segs.p: ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti.
Imassa khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamatha;
segs.e: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” replied those mendicants. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti, tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
“tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe …pe…
yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe”ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipucchimha.
Tesaṁ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi, imehi padehi, imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto”ti.
segs.e: Then they said, “And Ānanda explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”
“Mendicants, Ānanda is astute, he has great wisdom.

segs.p: Mañcepi tumhe, bhikkhave, etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi taṁ evamevaṁ byākareyyaṁ yathā taṁ ānandena byākataṁ.
segs.e: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Ānanda.

segs.p: Eso cevetassa attho. Evañca naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”

12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
The Question of Sakka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Sakka, lord of gods, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

segs.p: “Santi kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Lord of gods, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”

12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
The Question of Pañcasikha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then the centaur Pañcasikha went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”
“Pañcasikha, there are sights known by the eye …

segs.p: santi kho, pañcasikha, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, pañcasikha, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, pañcasikha, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā …pe…
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye …

segs.p: santi kho, pañcasikha, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, pañcasikha, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”
Linked Discourses 35.120
12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
Sāriputta and the Protégé

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain mendicant went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “saddhivihāriko, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, a mendicant protégé of mine has resigned the training and returned to a lesser life.”

segs.p: “Evametaṁ, āvuso, hoti indriyesu aguttadvārassa, bhojane amattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttassa.
segs.e: “That’s how it is, reverend, when someone doesn’t guard the sense doors, eats too much, and is not committed to wakefulness.

segs.p: ‘So vatāvuso, bhikkhu indriyesu aguttadvāro bhojane amattaññū jāgariyaṁ ananuyutto yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ santānessatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for such a mendicant to maintain the full and pure spiritual life for the rest of their life.

segs.p: ‘So vatāvuso, bhikkhu indriyesu guttadvāro, bhojane mattaññū, jāgariyaṁ anuyutto yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ santānessatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: But it is quite possible for a mendicant to maintain the full and pure spiritual life for the rest of their life if they guard the sense doors, eat in moderation, and are committed to wakefulness.
And how does someone guard the sense doors?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with the eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ, cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṁ, manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, indriyesu guttadvāro hoti.
segs.e: That’s how someone guards the sense doors.
And how does someone eat in moderation?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṁ āhāreti:
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant reflects rationally on the food that they eat:

segs.p: ‘neva davāya, na madāya, na maṇḍanāya, na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṁsūparatiyā, brahmacariyānuggahāya. Iti purāṇañca vedanaṁ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṁ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati, anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhojane mattaññū hoti.
segs.e: That’s how someone eats in moderation.
And how is someone committed to wakefulness?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu divasaṁ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant practices walking and sitting meditation by day, purifying their mind from obstacles.

segs.p: Rattiyā paṭhamaṁ yāmaṁ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: In the first watch of the night, they continue to practice walking and sitting meditation.

segs.p: Rattiyā majjhimaṁ yāmaṁ dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappeti pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno, uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā.
segs.e: In the middle watch, they lie down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

segs.p: Rattiyā pacchimaṁ yāmaṁ paccuṭṭhāya caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: In the last watch, they get up and continue to practice walking and sitting meditation, purifying their mind from obstacles.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, jāgariyaṁ anuyutto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how someone is committed to wakefulness.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘indriyesu guttadvārā bhavissāma, bhojane mattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ anuyuttā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will guard the sense doors, eat in moderation, and be committed to wakefulness.’
That’s how you should train.”
Linked Discourses 35.121
12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
Advice to Rāhula

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,
“The qualities that ripen in freedom have ripened in Rāhula.

segs.p: yannūnāhaṁ rāhulaṁ uttariṁ āsavānaṁ khaye vineyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I lead him further to the ending of defilements?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, wandered for alms in Sāvatthī.
After the meal, on his return from almsround, he addressed Venerable Rāhula,
“Rāhula, get your sitting cloth.
Let’s go to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato paṭissutvā nisīdanaṁ ādāya bhagavantaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Rāhula. Taking his sitting cloth he followed behind the Buddha.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena anekāni devatāsahassāni bhagavantaṁ anubandhāni honti:
segs.e: Now at that time many thousands of deities followed the Buddha, thinking,

segs.p: “ajja bhagavā āyasmantaṁ rāhulaṁ uttariṁ āsavānaṁ khaye vinessatī”ti.
segs.e: “Today the Buddha will lead Rāhula further to the ending of defilements!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā andhavanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha plunged deep into the Dark Forest and sat at the root of a tree on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Āyasmāpi kho rāhulo bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Rāhula bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rāhulaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him:
“What do you think, Rāhula?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Are sights …
eye consciousness …
eye contact permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …

segs.p: “Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ, saññāgataṁ, saṅkhāragataṁ, viññāṇagataṁ, tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “Anything included in feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that arises dependent on eye contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: “Yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ, saññāgataṁ, saṅkhāragataṁ, viññāṇagataṁ, tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
“Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
“Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:

segs.e: mind permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Are ideas …
mind consciousness …
mind contact permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …

segs.p: “Yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ, saññāgataṁ, saṅkhāragataṁ, viññāṇagataṁ, tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “Anything included in feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, rāhula, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ tasmimpi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with anything included in feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: jivhāyapi nibbindati, rasesupi nibbindati, jivhāviññāṇepi nibbindati, jivhāsamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ tasmimpi nibbindati …pe….
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Manasmimpi nibbindati, dhammesupi nibbindati, manoviññāṇepi nibbindati, manosamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact. And they grow disillusioned with anything included in feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that arises dependent on mind contact.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandi.
segs.e: Satisfied, Venerable Rāhula approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne āyasmato rāhulassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucci.
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, Rāhula’s mind was freed from defilements by not grasping.

segs.p: Anekānañca devatāsahassānaṁ virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
segs.e: And the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in those thousands of deities:
“Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
Things That Tighten Fetters
“Mendicants, I will teach you the things that tighten the fetters, and the fetter.
Listen …

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, saṁyojaniyā dhammā, katamañca saṁyojanaṁ?
segs.e: What are the things that tighten the fetters? And what is the fetter?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
These are called the things that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Yo tattha chandarāgo, taṁ tattha saṁyojanaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The desire and greed for them is the fetter.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: thoughts known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
These are called the things that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Yo tattha chandarāgo taṁ tattha saṁyojanan”ti.
segs.e: The desire and greed for them is the fetter.”
Linked Discourses 35.123
12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation
Things That Fuel Grasping
“Mendicants, I will teach you the things that fuel grasping, and the grasping.
Listen …

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, upādāniyā dhammā, katamañca upādānaṁ?
segs.e: What are the things that fuel grasping? And what is the grasping?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
These are called the things that fuel grasping.

segs.p: Yo tattha chandarāgo, taṁ tattha upādānaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The desire and greed for them is the grasping.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
These are called the things that fuel grasping.

segs.p: Yo tattha chandarāgo taṁ tattha upādānan”ti.
segs.e: The desire and greed for them is the grasping.”
Linked Discourses 35.124
13. Householders
At Vesālī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho uggo gahapati vesāliko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho uggo gahapati vesāliko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Ugga of Vesālī went up to the Buddha, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

segs.p: “Santi kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Householder, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato. Na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”

13. Householders
In the Land of the Vajjis

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati hatthigāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Vajjis at Elephant Village.

segs.p: Atha kho uggo gahapati hatthigāmako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho uggo gahapati hatthigāmako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Uggata of Elephant Village went up to the Buddha, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?
