13. Householders
At Nāḷandā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṁ viharati pāvārikambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho, upāli gahapati, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho, upāli gahapati, bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Upāli went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?” …
(Tell in full as in SN 35.124.)

segs.p: “Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.127
13. Householders
With Bhāradvāja

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho rājā udeno yenāyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā piṇḍolabhāradvājena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then King Udena went up to Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā udeno āyasmantaṁ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho bhāradvāja, hetu ko paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikīḷitāvino kāmesu yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ caranti, addhānañca āpādentī”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Bhāradvāja, there are these young monks who are youthful, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life; and they’ve never played around with sensual pleasures. What is the cause, what is the reason why they practice the full and pure spiritual life as long as they live, maintaining it for a long time?”

segs.p: “Vuttaṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena:
segs.e: “Great king, this has been stated by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha:

segs.p: ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, mātumattīsu mātucittaṁ upaṭṭhapetha, bhaginimattīsu bhaginicittaṁ upaṭṭhapetha, dhītumattīsu dhītucittaṁ upaṭṭhapethā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Please, monks, think of women your mother’s age as your mother. Think of women your sister’s age as your sister. And think of women your daughter’s age as your daughter.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, mahārāja, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikīḷitāvino kāmesu yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ caranti, addhānañca āpādentī”ti.
segs.e: This is a cause, Great King, this is a reason why these young monks practice the full and pure spiritual life as long as they live, maintaining it for a long time.”
“But worthy Bhāradvāja, the mind is wanton.

segs.p: Appekadā mātumattīsupi lobhadhammā uppajjanti, bhaginimattīsupi lobhadhammā uppajjanti, dhītumattīsupi lobhadhammā uppajjanti.
segs.e: Sometimes thoughts of desire come up even for women your mother’s age, your sister’s age, or your daughter’s age.

segs.p: Atthi nu kho, bho bhāradvāja, añño ca hetu, añño ca paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā …pe… addhānañca āpādentī”ti?
segs.e: Is there another cause, another reason why these young monks live the full and pure spiritual life for their entire life?”

segs.p: “Vuttaṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena:
segs.e: “Great king, this has been stated by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha:

segs.p: ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, imameva kāyaṁ uddhaṁ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṁ pūraṁ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhatha—
segs.e: ‘Please, monks, examine your own body up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth.

segs.p: atthi imasmiṁ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṁsaṁ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṁ vakkaṁ hadayaṁ yakanaṁ kilomakaṁ pihakaṁ papphāsaṁ antaṁ antaguṇaṁ udariyaṁ karīsaṁ pittaṁ semhaṁ pubbo lohitaṁ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttan’ti.
segs.e: In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’

segs.p: Ayampi kho, mahārāja, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā …pe… addhānañca āpādentī”ti.
segs.e: This is also a cause, Great King, this is a reason why these young monks live the full and pure spiritual life for their entire life, maintaining it for a long time.”

segs.p: “Ye te, bho bhāradvāja, bhikkhū bhāvitakāyā bhāvitasīlā bhāvitacittā bhāvitapaññā, tesaṁ taṁ sukaraṁ hoti.
segs.e: “This is easy to do for those mendicants who have developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Ye ca kho te, bho bhāradvāja, bhikkhū abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā, tesaṁ taṁ dukkaraṁ hoti.
segs.e: But it’s hard to do for those mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Appekadā, bho bhāradvāja, asubhato manasi karissāmīti subhatova āgacchati.
segs.e: Sometimes I plan to focus on something as ugly, but only its beauty comes to mind.

segs.p: Atthi nu kho, bho bhāradvāja, añño ca kho hetu añño ca paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā …pe… addhānañca āpādentī”ti?
segs.e: Is there another cause, another reason why these young monks live the full and pure spiritual life for their entire life?”

segs.p: “Vuttaṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena:
segs.e: “Great king, this has been stated by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha:
‘Please, monks, live with sense doors guarded.

segs.p: Cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā mā nimittaggāhino ahuvattha, mānubyañjanaggāhino.
segs.e: When you see a sight with your eyes, don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjatha. Rakkhatha cakkhundriyaṁ; cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjatha.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, practice restraint, protect the faculty of sight, and achieve its restraint.
When you hear a sound with your ears …
When you smell an odor with your nose …
When you taste a flavor with your tongue …
When you feel a touch with your body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya mā nimittaggāhino ahuvattha, mānubyañjanaggāhino.
segs.e: When you know an idea with your mind, don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjatha. Rakkhatha manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjathā’ti.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, practice restraint, protect the faculty of mind, and achieve its restraint.’

segs.p: Ayampi kho, mahārāja, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikīḷitāvino kāmesu yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ caranti, addhānañca āpādentī”ti.
segs.e: This is also a cause, Great King, this is a reason why these young monks practice the full and pure spiritual life as long as they live, maintaining it for a long time.”
“It’s incredible, worthy Bhāradvāja, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāva subhāsitañcidaṁ, bho bhāradvāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena.
segs.e: How well this was said by the Buddha!

segs.p: Esova kho, bho bhāradvāja, hetu, esa paccayo yenime daharā bhikkhū susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikīḷitāvino kāmesu yāvajīvaṁ paripuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ caranti, addhānañca āpādentīti.
segs.e: This is the real cause, this is the reason why these young monks practice the full and pure spiritual life as long as they live, maintaining it for a long time.

segs.p: Ahampi kho, bho bhāradvāja, yasmiṁ samaye arakkhiteneva kāyena, arakkhitāya vācāya, arakkhitena cittena, anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā, asaṁvutehi indriyehi antepuraṁ pavisāmi, ativiya maṁ tasmiṁ samaye lobhadhammā parisahanti.
segs.e: For sometimes I too enter the harem with unprotected body, speech, mind, mindfulness, and sense faculties. At those times powerful thoughts of desire get the better of me.

segs.p: Yasmiñca khvāhaṁ, bho bhāradvāja, samaye rakkhiteneva kāyena, rakkhitāya vācāya, rakkhitena cittena, upaṭṭhitāya satiyā, saṁvutehi indriyehi antepuraṁ pavisāmi, na maṁ tathā tasmiṁ samaye lobhadhammā parisahanti.
segs.e: But sometimes I enter the harem with protected body, speech, mind, mindfulness, and sense faculties. At those times such thoughts of desire don’t get the better of me.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho bhāradvāja, abhikkantaṁ, bho bhāradvāja.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Bhāradvāja! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho bhāradvāja, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā bhāradvājena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the worthy Bhāradvāja has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bho bhāradvāja, taṁ bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ bhāradvājo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Bhāradvāja remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 35.128
13. Householders
With Soṇa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho soṇo gahapatiputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho soṇo gahapatiputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Soṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?” …
(Tell in full as in SN 35.118.)

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, soṇa, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantīti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 35.129
13. Householders
With Ghosita

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho ghosito gahapati yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho ghosito gahapati āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Ghosita went up to Venerable Ānanda, and said to him:
“Honorable Ānanda, they speak of ‘the diversity of elements’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: In what way did the Buddha speak of the diversity of elements?”

segs.p: “Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, cakkhudhātu, rūpā ca manāpā, cakkhuviññāṇañca sukhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: “Householder, the eye element is found, as are agreeable sights, and eye consciousness.
Pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, cakkhudhātu, rūpā ca amanāpā, cakkhuviññāṇañca dukkhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: The eye element is found, as are disagreeable sights, and eye consciousness.
Painful feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, cakkhudhātu, rūpā ca manāpā upekkhāvedaniyā, cakkhuviññāṇañca adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: The eye element is found, as are sights that are a basis for equanimity, and eye consciousness.
Neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, jivhādhātu, rasā ca manāpā, jivhāviññāṇañca sukhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, jivhādhātu, rasā ca amanāpā, jivhāviññāṇañca dukkhavedaniyaṁ.
Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, jivhādhātu, rasā ca upekkhāvedaniyā, jivhāviññāṇañca adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ.
saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, manodhātu, dhammā ca manāpā, manoviññāṇañca sukhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: mind element is found, as are agreeable ideas, and mind consciousness.
Pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, manodhātu, dhammā ca amanāpā, manoviññāṇañca dukkhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: The mind element is found, as are disagreeable ideas, and mind consciousness.
Painful feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho, gahapati, manodhātu, dhammā ca upekkhāvedaniyā, manoviññāṇañca adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ.
segs.e: The mind element is found, as are ideas that are a basis for equanimity, and mind consciousness.
Neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: This is how the Buddha spoke of the diversity of elements.”
Linked Discourses 35.130
13. Householders
With Hāliddikāni

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati kuraraghare papāte pabbate.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying in the land of the Avantis near Kuraraghara on Steep Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho hāliddikāni gahapati yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho hāliddikāni gahapati āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Hāliddikāni went up to Venerable Mahākaccāna … and asked him,
“Sir, this was said by the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘dhātunānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṁ; phassanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Diversity of elements gives rise to diversity of contacts, and diversity of contacts gives rise to diversity of feelings.’

segs.p: Kathaṁ nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṁ; phassanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattan”ti?
segs.e: How does diversity of elements give rise to diversity of contacts, and diversity of contacts gives rise to diversity of feelings?”

segs.p: “Idha, gahapati, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā ‘manāpaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti cakkhuviññāṇaṁ sukhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: “Householder, it’s when a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes and understands it to be agreeable.
There is eye consciousness; and pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Cakkhunā kho paneva rūpaṁ disvā ‘amanāpaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti cakkhuviññāṇaṁ dukkhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: Then they see a sight and understand it to be disagreeable.
There is eye consciousness; and painful feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

segs.p: Cakkhunā kho paneva rūpaṁ disvā ‘upekkhāṭṭhāniyaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti cakkhuviññāṇaṁ adukkhamasukhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: Then they see a sight and understand it to be a basis for equanimity.
There is eye consciousness; and neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, bhikkhu sotena saddaṁ sutvā …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant hears a sound with their ears …
smells an odor with their nose …
tastes a flavor with their tongue …
encounters a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya ‘manāpaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti manoviññāṇaṁ sukhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind and understands it to be agreeable.
There is mind consciousness; and pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Manasā kho paneva dhammaṁ viññāya ‘amanāpaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti manoviññāṇaṁ dukkhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: Then they know an idea and understand it to be disagreeable.
There is mind consciousness; and painful feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

segs.p: Manasā kho paneva dhammaṁ viññāya ‘upekkhāṭṭhāniyaṁ itthetan’ti pajānāti manoviññāṇaṁ adukkhamasukhavedaniyañca.
segs.e: Then they know an idea and understand it to be a basis for equanimity.
Neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṁ; phassanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattan”ti.
segs.e: That’s how diversity of elements gives rise to diversity of contacts, and diversity of contacts gives rise to diversity of feelings.”
Linked Discourses 35.131
13. Householders
Nakula’s Father

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho nakulapitā gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho nakulapitā gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Nakula’s father went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

segs.p: “Santi kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: “Householder, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: Santi ca kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.
There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ nābhinandato nābhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.
A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”
Linked Discourses 35.132
13. Householders
With Lohicca

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati makkarakate araññakuṭikāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying in the land of the Avantis in a wilderness hut near Makkarakaṭa.

segs.p: Atha kho lohiccassa brāhmaṇassa sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā yenāyasmato mahākaccānassa araññakuṭikā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā parito parito kuṭikāya anucaṅkamanti anuvicaranti uccāsaddā mahāsaddā kānici kānici seleyyakāni karonti:
segs.e: Then several students, pupils of the brahmin Lohicca, approached Mahākaccāna’s wilderness hut while collecting firewood. They walked and wandered all around the hut, making a colossal racket and all kinds of jeers:

segs.p: “ime pana muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kaṇhā bandhupādāpaccā, imesaṁ bharatakānaṁ sakkatā garukatā mānitā pūjitā apacitā”ti.
segs.e: “These shavelings, fake ascetics, primitives, black spawn from the feet of our kinsman, the Lord! They’re honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by so-called inheritors of Vedic culture.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākaccāno vihārā nikkhamitvā te māṇavake etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahākaccāna left his dwelling and said to those young students,
“Young students, stop being so noisy.
I will speak to you on the teaching.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, te māṇavakā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: When this was said, the young students fell silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākaccāno te māṇavake gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Mahākaccāna recited these verses for them:
“For the brahmins of old, ethics were the highest;
they remembered the ancient legends.
Their sense doors were guarded, well protected,
and they had mastered anger.

segs.p: Dhamme ca jhāne ca ratā ahesuṁ,
segs.e: Those brahmins who remembered <j>the ancient legends
enjoyed virtue and absorption.
But these have lost their way. <j>Saying, ‘We must pray’,
they live out of balance, judging by clan.
Mastered by anger, they take up many arms,
indifferent to those with craving and without.
All is vain for someone <j>who doesn’t guard the sense doors,
like the wealth a person finds in a dream.
Fasting, sleeping on bare ground,
bathing at daybreak, the three Vedas,
rough hides, dreadlocks, and mud,
hymns, precepts and observances, <j>and fervent austerities,
fawning, bent staffs,
and sipping water.
These emblems of the brahmins
are only used to generate profits.
A mind that’s serene,
clear and unclouded,
kind to all creatures:
that’s the path to attainment of divinity!”

segs.p: Atha kho te māṇavakā kupitā anattamanā yena lohicco brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā lohiccaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those young students, offended and upset, went to the brahmin Lohicca and said to him,

segs.p: “yagghe bhavaṁ jāneyya, samaṇo mahākaccāno brāhmaṇānaṁ mante ekaṁsena apavadati, paṭikkosatī”ti?
segs.e: “Please, master, you should know this. The ascetic Mahākaccāna condemns and rejects outright the hymns of the brahmins!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, lohicco brāhmaṇo kupito ahosi anattamano.
segs.e: When they said this, Lohicca was offended and upset.
Then he thought,

segs.p: “na kho pana metaṁ patirūpaṁ yohaṁ aññadatthu māṇavakānaṁyeva sutvā samaṇaṁ mahākaccānaṁ akkoseyyaṁ paribhāseyyaṁ.
segs.e: “But it wouldn’t be appropriate for me to abuse or insult the ascetic Mahākaccāna solely because of what I’ve heard from these young students.
Why don’t I go and ask him about it?”

segs.p: Atha kho lohicco brāhmaṇo tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Lohicca together with those young students went to Venerable Mahākaccāna and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho lohicco brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him,

segs.p: “āgamaṁsu nu khvidha, bho kaccāna, amhākaṁ sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā”ti?
segs.e: “Master Kaccāna, did several young pupils of mine come by here collecting firewood?”

segs.p: “Āgamaṁsu khvidha te, brāhmaṇa, sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā”ti.
segs.e: “They did, brahmin.”

segs.p: “Ahu pana bhoto kaccānassa tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti?
segs.e: “But did you have some discussion with them?”

segs.p: “Ahu kho me, brāhmaṇa, tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ kocideva kathāsallāpo”ti.
segs.e: “I did.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana bhoto kaccānassa tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ ahosi kathāsallāpo”ti?
segs.e: “But what kind of discussion did you have with them?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ kho me, brāhmaṇa, tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ ahosi kathāsallāpo:
segs.e: “This is the discussion I had with these young students.” And he repeated the verses in full.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho me, brāhmaṇa, tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ ahosi kathāsallāpo”ti.

segs.e: “Worthy Kaccāna spoke of someone who doesn’t guard the sense doors.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bho kaccāna, aguttadvāro hotī”ti?
segs.e: How do you define someone who doesn’t guard the sense doors?”

segs.p: “Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā piyarūpe rūpe adhimuccati, appiyarūpe rūpe byāpajjati, anupaṭṭhitakāyassati ca viharati, parittacetaso
segs.e: “Brahmin, take someone who sees a sight with their eyes. If it’s pleasant they hold on to it, but if it’s unpleasant they dislike it. They live with mindfulness of the body unestablished and their heart stunted.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya piyarūpe dhamme adhimuccati, appiyarūpe ca dhamme byāpajjati, anupaṭṭhitakāyassati ca viharati, parittacetaso
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, if it’s pleasant they hold on to it, but if it’s unpleasant they dislike it. They live with mindfulness of the body unestablished and their heart stunted.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.
That’s how someone doesn’t guard the sense doors.”
“It’s incredible, worthy Kaccāna, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ bhotā kaccānena aguttadvārova samāno aguttadvāroti akkhāto.
segs.e: How accurately you’ve explained someone whose sense doors are unguarded!
You also spoke of someone who does guard the sense doors.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bho kaccāna, guttadvāro hotī”ti?
segs.e: How do you define someone who does guard the sense doors?”

segs.p: “Idha, brāhmaṇa, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā piyarūpe rūpe nādhimuccati, appiyarūpe rūpe na byāpajjati, upaṭṭhitakāyassati ca viharati, appamāṇacetaso
segs.e: “Brahmin, take a mendicant who sees a sight with their eyes. If it’s pleasant they don’t hold on to it, and if it’s unpleasant they don’t dislike it. They live with mindfulness of the body established and a limitless heart.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya piyarūpe dhamme nādhimuccati, appiyarūpe dhamme na byāpajjati, upaṭṭhitakāyassati ca viharati, appamāṇacetaso
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, if it’s pleasant they don’t hold on to it, and if it’s unpleasant they don’t dislike it. They live with mindfulness of the body established and a limitless heart.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.
That’s how someone guards the sense doors.”
“It’s incredible, worthy Kaccāna, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ bhotā kaccānena guttadvārova samāno guttadvāroti akkhāto.
segs.e: How accurately you’ve explained someone whose sense doors are guarded!

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho kaccāna; abhikkantaṁ, bho kaccāna.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Kaccāna! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho kaccāna, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā kaccānena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the worthy Kaccāna has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bho kaccāna, taṁ bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ kaccāno dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gataṁ.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Kaccāna remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.

segs.p: Yathā ca bhavaṁ kaccāno makkarakate upāsakakulāni upasaṅkamati; evameva lohiccakulaṁ upasaṅkamatu.
segs.e: Please come to my family just as you go to the families of the lay followers in Makkarakaṭa.

segs.p: Tattha ye māṇavakā vā māṇavikā vā bhavantaṁ kaccānaṁ abhivādessanti paccuṭṭhissanti āsanaṁ vā udakaṁ vā dassanti, tesaṁ taṁ bhavissati dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: The brahmin boys and girls there will bow to you, rise in your presence, and give you a seat and water. That will be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”
Linked Discourses 35.133
13. Householders
Verahaccāni

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā udāyī kāmaṇḍāyaṁ viharati todeyyassa brāhmaṇassa ambavane.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Udāyī was staying near Kāmaṇḍā in the brahmin Todeyya’s mango grove.

segs.p: Atha kho verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā antevāsī māṇavako yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā udāyinā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a boy who was a pupil of the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan went up to Udāyī and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho taṁ māṇavakaṁ āyasmā udāyī dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
segs.e: Udāyī educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired that young student with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Atha kho so māṇavako āyasmatā udāyinā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā yena verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā verahaccānigottaṁ brāhmaṇiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then that young student went to the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan and said to her,
“Please, madam, you should know this.

segs.p: Samaṇo udāyī dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ, sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsetī”ti.
segs.e: The ascetic Udāyī teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.”

segs.p: “Tena hi tvaṁ, māṇavaka, mama vacanena samaṇaṁ udāyiṁ nimantehi svātanāya bhattenā”ti.
segs.e: “Then, young student, invite him in my name for tomorrow’s meal.”
segs.s: the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhotī”ti kho so māṇavako verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā paṭissutvā yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, madam,” he replied. He went to Udāyī and said,

segs.p: “adhivāsetu kira, bhavaṁ udāyī amhākaṁ ācariyabhariyāya verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā svātanāya bhattan”ti.
segs.e: “Would Worthy Udāyī please accept an offering of tomorrow’s meal from my tutor’s wife, the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan?”
Udāyī consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā udāyī tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then when the night had passed, Udāyī robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the brahmin lady’s home, and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin lady served and satisfied Udāyī with her own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ pādukā ārohitvā ucce āsane nisīditvā sīsaṁ oguṇṭhitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When Udāyī had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, she put on a pair of slippers, sat on a high seat, covered her head, and said to him,
“Ascetic, preach the Dhamma.”
“There will be an occasion for that, sister,” he replied, then rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho so māṇavako yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā udāyinā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: For a second time that young student went to Venerable Udāyī …

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho taṁ māṇavakaṁ āyasmā udāyī dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.

Dutiyampi kho so māṇavako āyasmatā udāyinā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā yena verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā verahaccānigottaṁ brāhmaṇiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a second time that young student went to the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan …

segs.p: Samaṇo udāyī dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ, sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsetī”ti.
“Evamevaṁ pana tvaṁ, māṇavaka, samaṇassa udāyissa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsasi.
segs.e: She said to him, “You keep praising the ascetic Udāyī like this.

segs.p: Samaṇo panudāyī ‘bhaṇa, samaṇa, dhamman’ti vutto samāno ‘bhavissati, bhagini, samayo’ti vatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto”ti.
segs.e: But when I asked him to preach the Dhamma he just said that there would be an occasion for that, and then he got up and left.”

segs.p: “Tathā hi pana tvaṁ, bhoti, pādukā ārohitvā ucce āsane nisīditvā sīsaṁ oguṇṭhitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: “Madam, that’s because you put on a pair of slippers, sat on a high seat, and covered your head before inviting him to teach.
For the good sirs respect the teaching.”

segs.p: “Tena hi tvaṁ, māṇavaka, mama vacanena samaṇaṁ udāyiṁ nimantehi svātanāya bhattenā”ti.
segs.e: “Then, young student, invite him in my name for tomorrow’s meal.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhotī”ti kho so māṇavako verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā paṭissutvā yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, madam,” he replied. …

segs.p: “adhivāsetu kira bhavaṁ udāyī amhākaṁ ācariyabhariyāya verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā svātanāya bhattan”ti.
Atha kho āyasmā udāyī tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena verahaccānigottāya brāhmaṇiyā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
Atha kho verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin lady served and satisfied Udāyī with her own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ pādukā orohitvā nīce āsane nisīditvā sīsaṁ vivaritvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When Udāyī had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, she took off her slippers, sat on a low seat, uncovered her head, and said to him,

segs.p: “kismiṁ nu kho, bhante, sati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, kismiṁ asati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ na paññapentī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, when what exists do the perfected ones assert that there is pleasure and pain? When what doesn’t exist do the perfected ones not declare that there is pleasure and pain?”

segs.p: “Cakkhusmiṁ kho, bhagini, sati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, cakkhusmiṁ asati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ na paññapenti …pe…
segs.e: “Sister, when there’s an eye, the perfected ones assert that there is pleasure and pain. When there’s no eye, the perfected ones don’t declare that there is pleasure and pain.

segs.p: jivhāya sati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, jivhāya asati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ na paññapenti …pe….
segs.e: When there’s an ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Manasmiṁ sati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ paññapenti, manasmiṁ asati arahanto sukhadukkhaṁ na paññapentī”ti.
segs.e: mind, the perfected ones assert that there is pleasure and pain. When there’s no mind, the perfected ones don’t declare that there is pleasure and pain.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, verahaccānigottā brāhmaṇī āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin lady said to Udāyī,
“Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ ayyena udāyinā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, Master Udāyī has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, ayya udāyi, taṁ bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsikaṁ maṁ ayyo udāyī dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may Master Udāyī remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

14. At Devadaha
At Devadaha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati devadahaṁ nāma sakyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near the Sakyan town named Devadaha.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sabbesaṁyeva bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu appamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmi, na ca panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sabbesaṁyeva bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu nāppamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: “When it comes to the six fields of contact, mendicants, I don’t say that all mendicants have work to do with diligence, nor do I say that none of them have work to do with diligence.

segs.p: Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojanā sammadaññāvimuttā, tesāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu nāppamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: I say that, when it comes to the six fields of contact, mendicants don’t have work to do with diligence if they are perfected, with defilements ended, having completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and become rightly freed through enlightenment.
Why is that?

segs.p: Kataṁ tesaṁ appamādena, abhabbā te pamajjituṁ.
segs.e: They’ve done their work with diligence, and are incapable of negligence.

segs.p: Ye ca kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sekkhā appattamānasā anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ patthayamānā viharanti, tesāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu appamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: I say that, when it comes to the six fields of contact, mendicants do have work to do with diligence if they are trainees, who haven’t achieved their heart’s desire, but live aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
Why is that?

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā manoramāpi, amanoramāpi.
segs.e: There are sights known by the eye that are pleasant and also those that are unpleasant.

segs.p: Tyāssa phussa phussa cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Though experiencing them again and again they don’t occupy the mind.

segs.p: Cetaso apariyādānā āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṁ cittaṁ ekaggaṁ.
segs.e: Their energy is roused up and unflagging, their mindfulness is established and lucid, their body is tranquil and undisturbed, and their mind is immersed and unified in samādhi.

segs.p: Imaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appamādaphalaṁ sampassamāno tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu appamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmi …pe…
segs.e: Seeing this fruit of diligence, I say that those mendicants have work to do with diligence when it comes to the six fields of contact. …

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā manoramāpi amanoramāpi.
segs.e: There are ideas known by the mind that are pleasant and also those that are unpleasant.

segs.p: Tyāssa phussa phussa cittaṁ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti.
segs.e: Though experiencing them again and again they don’t occupy the mind.

segs.p: Cetaso apariyādānā āraddhaṁ hoti vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṁ cittaṁ ekaggaṁ.
segs.e: Their energy is roused up and unflagging, their mindfulness is established and lucid, their body is tranquil and undisturbed, and their mind is immersed and unified in samādhi.

segs.p: Imaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, appamādaphalaṁ sampassamāno tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ chasu phassāyatanesu appamādena karaṇīyanti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Seeing this fruit of diligence, I say that those mendicants have work to do with diligence when it comes to the six fields of contact.”

Opportunity
“You’re fortunate, mendicants, so very fortunate,
to have the opportunity to lead the spiritual life.

segs.p: Diṭṭhā mayā, bhikkhave, chaphassāyatanikā nāma nirayā.

segs.p: Tattha yaṁ kiñci cakkhunā rūpaṁ passati aniṭṭharūpaṁyeva passati, no iṭṭharūpaṁ; akantarūpaṁyeva passati, no kantarūpaṁ; amanāparūpaṁyeva passati, no manāparūpaṁ.
segs.e: There, whatever sight you see with your eye is unlikable, not likable; undesirable, not desirable; unpleasant, not pleasant.
Whatever sound you hear …
Whatever odor you smell …
Whatever flavor you taste …
Whatever touch you feel …

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci manasā dhammaṁ vijānāti aniṭṭharūpaṁyeva vijānāti, no iṭṭharūpaṁ; akantarūpaṁyeva vijānāti, no kantarūpaṁ; amanāparūpaṁyeva vijānāti, no manāparūpaṁ.
segs.e: Whatever idea you know with your mind is unlikable, not likable; undesirable, not desirable; unpleasant, not pleasant.

segs.p: Lābhā vo, bhikkhave, suladdhaṁ vo, bhikkhave,
segs.e: You’re fortunate, mendicants, so very fortunate,
to have the opportunity to lead the spiritual life.

segs.p: Diṭṭhā mayā, bhikkhave, chaphassāyatanikā nāma saggā.
segs.e: I’ve seen the heaven called ‘Related to the Six Fields of Contact’.

14. At Devadaha
Liking Sights (1st)
“Mendicants, gods and humans like sights, they love them and enjoy them.
But when sights perish, fade away, and cease, gods and humans live in suffering.
Gods and humans like sounds …
smells …
tastes …
touches …
ideas, they love them and enjoy them.
But when ideas perish, fade away, and cease, gods and humans live in suffering.

segs.p: Tathāgato ca kho, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho rūpānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā na rūpārāmo na rūparato na rūpasammudito.
segs.e: The Realized One has truly understood the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape of sights, so he doesn’t like, love, or enjoy them.
When sights perish, fade away, and cease, the Realized One lives happily.
The Realized One has truly understood the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape of sounds …
smells …
tastes …
touches …

segs.p: dhammānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā na dhammārāmo, na dhammarato, na dhammasammudito.
segs.e: ideas, so he doesn’t like, love, or enjoy them.
When ideas perish, fade away, and cease, the Realized One lives happily.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Sights, sounds, tastes, smells,
touches and ideas, the lot of them—
they’re likable, desirable, and pleasurable
as long as you can say that they exist.
For all the world with its gods,
this is what they deem happiness.
And where they cease
is deemed as suffering for them.
The noble ones have seen that happiness
is the cessation of substantial reality.
This insight by those who see
contradicts the whole world.
What others say is happiness
the noble ones say is suffering.
What others say is suffering
the noble ones know as happiness.
See, this teaching is hard to understand,
it confuses the ignorant.
There is darkness for the shrouded;
blackness for those who don’t see.
But the good are open;
like light for those who see.
Though close, they do not understand,
the seekers inexpert in the teaching.
They’re mired in desire for continued existence,
flowing along the stream of lives,
mired in Māra’s dominion:
this teaching isn’t easy for them to understand.
Who, apart from the noble ones,
is qualified to understand this state?
Having rightly understood this state,
the undefiled are fully extinguished.”

14. At Devadaha
Not Yours (1st)
“Mendicants, give up what’s not yours.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
And what isn’t yours?

segs.p: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṁ; taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: The eye isn’t yours: give it up.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati …pe…
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Sā vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissati …pe…

segs.e: mind isn’t yours: give it up.

segs.p: So vo pahīno hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṁ imasmiṁ jetavane tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṁ taṁ jano hareyya vā ḍaheyya vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā kareyya, api nu tumhākaṁ evamassa:
segs.e: Suppose a person was to carry off the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves in this Jeta’s Grove, or burn them, or do what they want with them. Would you think:

segs.p: ‘amhe jano harati vā ḍahati vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karotī’”ti?
segs.e: ‘This person is carrying us off, burning us, or doing what they want with us’?”
“No, sir.
Why is that?

segs.p: “Na hi no etaṁ, bhante, attā vā attaniyaṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: Because  to us that’s neither self nor belonging to self.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cakkhu na tumhākaṁ; taṁ pajahatha.
segs.e: “In the same way, the eye isn’t yours: give it up.

segs.p: Taṁ vo pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati …pe…
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.
The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Sā vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissati …pe…

segs.e: mind isn’t yours: give it up.

segs.p: So vo pahīno hitāya sukhāya bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: Giving it up will be for your welfare and happiness.”

14. At Devadaha
Interior and Cause Are Impermanent
“Mendicants, the eye is impermanent.

segs.p: Yopi hetu, yopi paccayo cakkhussa uppādāya, sopi anicco.
segs.e: The cause and reason that gives rise to the eye is also impermanent.

segs.p: Aniccasambhūtaṁ, bhikkhave, cakkhu kuto niccaṁ bhavissati …pe…
segs.e: Since the eye is produced by what is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: Yopi hetu, yopi paccayo jivhāya uppādāya sopi anicco.
Aniccasambhūtā, bhikkhave, jivhā kuto niccā bhavissati …pe…

segs.e: mind is impermanent.

segs.p: Yopi, bhikkhave, hetu yopi paccayo manassa uppādāya, sopi anicco.
segs.e: The cause and reason that gives rise to the mind is also impermanent.

segs.p: Aniccasambhūto, bhikkhave, mano kuto nicco bhavissati.
segs.e: Since the mind is produced by what is impermanent, how could it be permanent?

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati …pe… jivhāyapi nibbindati …pe… manasmimpi nibbindati,
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

segs.p: nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

15. The Old and the New
The Cessation of Deeds

segs.p: “Navapurāṇāni, bhikkhave, kammāni desessāmi kammanirodhaṁ kammanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you old deeds, new deeds, the cessation of deeds, and the practice that leads to the cessation of deeds.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmīti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …
And what is old deeds?

segs.p: Cakkhu, bhikkhave, purāṇakammaṁ abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ vedaniyaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ …pe…
segs.e: The eye is old deeds. It should be seen as produced by choices and intentions, as something to be felt.

segs.p: jivhā purāṇakammā abhisaṅkhatā abhisañcetayitā vedaniyā daṭṭhabbā …pe…
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: mano purāṇakammo abhisaṅkhato abhisañcetayito vedaniyo daṭṭhabbo.
segs.e: mind is old deeds. It should be seen as produced by choices and intentions, as something to be felt.
This is called old deeds.
And what is new deeds?

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, etarahi kammaṁ karoti kāyena vācāya manasā,
segs.e: The deeds you currently perform by way of body, speech, and mind.
These are called new deeds.
And what is the cessation of deeds?

segs.p: Yo kho, bhikkhave, kāyakammavacīkammamanokammassa nirodhā vimuttiṁ phusati,
segs.e: When you experience freedom due to the cessation of deeds by body, speech, and mind.
This is called the cessation of deeds.
And what’s the practice that leads to the cessation of deeds?
It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi—
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
This is called the practice that leads to the cessation of deeds.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, desitaṁ mayā purāṇakammaṁ, desitaṁ navakammaṁ, desito kammanirodho, desitā kammanirodhagāminī paṭipadā.
segs.e: So, mendicants, I’ve taught you old deeds, new deeds, the cessation of deeds, and the practice that leads to the cessation of deeds.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, satthārā karaṇīyaṁ sāvakānaṁ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya, kataṁ vo taṁ mayā.
segs.e: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

segs.p: Etāni, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha; mā pacchāvippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṁ vo amhākaṁ anusāsanī”ti.
segs.e: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicants! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”
Linked Discourses 35.147
15. The Old and the New
The Impermanent as Conducive to Extinguishment
“Mendicants, I will teach you a practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.
Listen …

segs.p: katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā?
segs.e: And what is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuṁ aniccanti passati, rūpā aniccāti passati, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ aniccanti passati, cakkhusamphasso aniccoti passati. Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccanti passati …pe…
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant sees that the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact are impermanent. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also impermanent.

segs.p: jivhā aniccāti passati, rasā aniccāti passati, jivhāviññāṇaṁ aniccanti passati, jivhāsamphasso aniccoti passati, yampidaṁ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccanti passati …pe…
segs.e: They see that the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: mano aniccoti passati, dhammā aniccāti passati, manoviññāṇaṁ aniccanti passati, manosamphasso aniccoti passati, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccanti passati.
segs.e: mind, ideas, mind-consciousness, and mind contact are impermanent. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also impermanent.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā”ti.
segs.e: This is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.”
Linked Discourses 35.148
15. The Old and the New
The Suffering as Conducive to Extinguishment
“Mendicants, I will teach you a practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.
Listen …

segs.p: katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā?
segs.e: And what is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, cakkhuṁ dukkhanti passati, rūpā dukkhāti passati, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ dukkhanti passati, cakkhusamphasso dukkhoti passati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhanti passati …pe…
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant sees that the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact are suffering. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also suffering.
They see that the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: mano dukkhoti passati, dhammā dukkhāti passati, manoviññāṇaṁ dukkhanti passati, manosamphasso dukkhoti passati, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhanti passati.
segs.e: mind, ideas, mind-consciousness, and mind contact are suffering. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also suffering.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā”ti.
segs.e: This is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.”

15. The Old and the New
Not-Self as Conducive to Extinguishment
“Mendicants, I will teach you a practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.
Listen …

segs.p: katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā?
segs.e: And what is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuṁ anattāti passati, rūpā anattāti passati, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ anattāti passati, cakkhusamphasso anattāti passati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anattāti passati …pe…
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant sees that the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact are not-self. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also not-self.

segs.p: mano anattāti passati, dhammā anattāti passati, manoviññāṇaṁ anattāti passati, manosamphasso anattāti passati, yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi anattāti passati.
segs.e: They see that the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind, ideas, mind-consciousness, and mind contact are not-self. And they see that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also not-self.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā”ti.
segs.e: This is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.”

15. The Old and the New
A Practice Conducive to Extinguishment
“Mendicants, I will teach you a practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.
Listen …

segs.p: katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā?
segs.e: And what is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment?
What do you think, mendicants?
Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Are sights …
eye consciousness …
eye contact …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.
Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. …
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, nibbānasappāyā paṭipadā”ti.
segs.e: This is that practice that’s conducive to extinguishment.”
Linked Discourses 35.151
15. The Old and the New
A Resident Pupil
“Mendicants, this spiritual life is lived without a resident pupil and without a teaching master.

segs.p: Santevāsiko, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sācariyako dukkhaṁ na phāsu viharati.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives with a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in suffering and discomfort.

segs.p: Anantevāsiko, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anācariyako sukhaṁ phāsu viharati.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives without a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in happiness and comfort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhu, santevāsiko sācariyako dukkhaṁ na phāsu viharati?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant who lives with a resident pupil and a teaching master live in suffering and discomfort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tyāssa anto vasanti, antassa vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities reside within. Since they have bad unskillful qualities residing within,
they’re said to have a resident pupil.

segs.p: Te naṁ samudācaranti, samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities master them. Since they’re mastered by bad unskillful qualities,
they’re said to have a teaching master.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Tyāssa anto vasanti, antassa vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
Te naṁ samudācaranti, samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti. Tasmā sācariyakoti vuccati …pe….
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind, bad, unskillful phenomena arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tyāssa anto vasanti, antassa vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities reside within. Since they have bad unskillful qualities residing within,
they’re said to have a resident pupil.

segs.p: Te naṁ samudācaranti, samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities master them. Since they’re mastered by bad unskillful qualities,
they’re said to have a teaching master.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santevāsiko sācariyako dukkhaṁ, na phāsu viharati.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant who lives with a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in suffering and discomfort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anantevāsiko anācariyako sukhaṁ phāsu viharati?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant who lives without a resident pupil and a teaching master live in happiness and comfort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, bad, unskillful phenomena don’t arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tyāssa na anto vasanti, nāssa anto vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities don’t reside within. Since they don’t have bad unskillful qualities residing within,
they’re said to not have a resident pupil.

segs.p: Te naṁ na samudācaranti, na samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities don’t master them. Since they’re not mastered by bad unskillful qualities,
they’re said to not have a teaching master.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā na uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears … smells … tastes … touches …

segs.p: Tyāssa na anto vasanti, nāssa anto vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
Te naṁ na samudācaranti, na samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti. Tasmā anācariyakoti vuccati …pe….
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā sarasaṅkappā saṁyojaniyā.
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind, bad, unskillful phenomena don’t arise: memories and thoughts that tighten the fetters.

segs.p: Tyāssa na anto vasanti, nāssa anto vasanti pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities don’t reside within. Since they don’t have bad unskillful qualities residing within,
they’re said to not have a resident pupil.

segs.p: Te naṁ na samudācaranti, na samudācaranti naṁ pāpakā akusalā dhammāti.
segs.e: Those qualities don’t master them. Since they’re not mastered by bad unskillful qualities,
they’re said to not have a teaching master.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anantevāsiko anācariyako sukhaṁ phāsu viharati.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant who lives without a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in happiness and comfort.
This spiritual life is lived without a resident pupil and without a teaching master.

segs.p: Anācariyakaṁ santevāsiko, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sācariyako dukkhaṁ, na phāsu viharati.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives with a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in suffering and discomfort.

segs.p: Anantevāsiko, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anācariyako sukhaṁ phāsu viharatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives without a resident pupil and a teaching master lives in happiness and comfort.”
Linked Discourses 35.152
15. The Old and the New
What’s the Goal of the Spiritual Life?

segs.p: “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:
‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: You should answer them:

segs.p: ‘dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand suffering.’

segs.p: Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

segs.p: ‘katamaṁ panāvuso, dukkhaṁ, yassa pariññāya samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṁ vussatī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Reverends, what is that suffering?’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyātha:
segs.e: You should answer them:
‘The eye is suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.
Sights …
Eye consciousness …
Eye contact …

segs.p: Yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ;
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.
The ear … nose … tongue … body …
mind …

segs.p: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi dukkhaṁ;
segs.e: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.
This is that suffering.
The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand this.’

segs.p: Evaṁ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ evaṁ byākareyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”
Linked Discourses 35.153
15. The Old and the New
Is There a Method?

segs.p: “Atthi nu kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya, aññatra ruciyā, aññatra anussavā, aññatra ākāraparivitakkā, aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Mendicants, is there a method—apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation—that a mendicant can rely on to declare their enlightenment? That is:

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti?
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā, bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṁyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “atthi, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya, aññatra ruciyā, aññatra anussavā, aññatra ākāraparivitakkā, aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “There is a method—apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation—that a mendicant can rely on to declare their enlightenment. That is:

segs.p: ‘“khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo, yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya …pe… aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākaroti: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti?
segs.e: And what is that method?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti;
segs.e: Take a mendicant who sees a sight with their eyes. When they have greed, hate, and delusion in them, they understand ‘I have greed, hate, and delusion in me.’

segs.p: asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti.
segs.e: When they don’t have greed, hate, and delusion in them, they understand ‘I don’t have greed, hate, and delusion in me.’

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti. Api nu me, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhāya vā veditabbā, ruciyā vā veditabbā, anussavena vā veditabbā, ākāraparivitakkena vā veditabbā, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā vā veditabbā”ti?
segs.e: Since this is so, are these things understood by faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation?”
“No, sir.”
“Aren’t they understood by seeing them with wisdom?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya, aññatra ruciyā, aññatra anussavā, aññatra ākāraparivitakkā, aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākaroti:
segs.e: “This is a method—apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation—that a mendicant can rely on to declare their enlightenment. That is:

segs.p: ‘“khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti pajānāmī’ti …pe….
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ …pe… rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … encounters a touch …

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; api nu me, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhāya vā veditabbā, ruciyā vā veditabbā, anussavena vā veditabbā, ākāraparivitakkena vā veditabbā, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā vā veditabbā”ti?

“Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya, aññatra ruciyā, aññatra anussavā, aññatra ākāraparivitakkā, aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākaroti: ‘“khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti pajānāmī’ti …pe….
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti;
segs.e: knows an idea with their mind. When they have greed, hate, and delusion in them, they understand ‘I have greed, hate, and delusion in me.’

segs.p: asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti.
segs.e: When they don’t have greed, hate, and delusion in them, they understand ‘I don’t have greed, hate, and delusion in me.’

segs.p: Yaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu manasā dhammaṁ viññāya santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohaṁ, natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgadosamohoti pajānāti; api nu me, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhāya vā veditabbā, ruciyā vā veditabbā, anussavena vā veditabbā, ākāraparivitakkena vā veditabbā, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā vā veditabbā”ti?
segs.e: Since this is so, are these things understood by faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation?”
“No, sir.”
“Aren’t they understood by seeing them with wisdom?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma bhikkhu aññatreva saddhāya, aññatra ruciyā, aññatra anussavā, aññatra ākāraparivitakkā, aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā aññaṁ byākaroti:
segs.e: “This too is a method—apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation—that a mendicant can rely on to declare their enlightenment. That is:

segs.p: ‘“khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”
Linked Discourses 35.154
15. The Old and the New
Endowed With Faculties

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,
“Sir, they speak of someone who is ‘accomplished in the faculties’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, indriyasampanno hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is someone accomplished in the faculties defined?”

segs.p: “Cakkhundriye ce, bhikkhu, udayabbayānupassī viharanto cakkhundriye nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicant, if someone meditates observing rise and fall in the eye faculty, they grow disillusioned with the eye faculty.

segs.p: jivhindriye ce, bhikkhu, udayabbayānupassī viharanto jivhindriye nibbindati …pe…
segs.e: If they meditate observing rise and fall in the ear faculty … nose faculty … tongue faculty … body faculty …

segs.p: manindriye ce, bhikkhu, udayabbayānupassī viharanto manindriye nibbindati.
segs.e: mind faculty, they grow disillusioned with the mind faculty.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati …pe… vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. … When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’
This is how someone who is accomplished in the faculties is defined.”

15. The Old and the New
A Dhamma Speaker

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,
“Sir, they speak of a ‘Dhamma speaker’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhammakathiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a Dhamma speaker defined?”

segs.p: “Cakkhussa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: “If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the eye, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Cakkhussa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the eye, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Cakkhussa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya …pe…
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the eye, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.

segs.p: jivhāya ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: manassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: mind, for its fading away and cessation, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Manassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the mind, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Manassa ce, bhikkhu, nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāyā”ti.
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the mind, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.”

16. The End of Relishing
The Interior and the End of Relishing

segs.p: “Aniccaṁyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuṁ aniccanti passati, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the eye really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.
Seeing rightly, they grow disillusioned.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is said to be well freed.

segs.p: aniccaṁyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu jivhaṁ aniccanti passati, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: The ear … nose … tongue … body …

segs.p: aniccaṁyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu manaṁ aniccanti passati, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: mind really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.
Seeing rightly, they grow disillusioned.
When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.
When relishing and greed end, the mind is said to be well freed.”
